Characters/Major-NPCs/Aegwynn.title: Aegwynn
Characters/Major-NPCs/Aegwynn.content:
Aegwynn


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A woman who held the world’s most dangerous office for nine hundred years, defied everyone, and was wrong about the one thing that mattered.


Guardian of Tirisfal for nearly nine centuries — longer than any other, and against the Council’s wishes for most of it.
She destroyed an avatar of Sargeras in Northrend and entombed it, believing she had won.
She is alive, elderly, in hiding, and carrying the knowledge that every war of the last thirty years is traceable to a decision she made alone.
Related
Guardians of Tirisfal · Medivh · Sargeras · Dark Portal · Kirin Tor · The First War

Characters/Major-NPCs/Alexstrasza.title: Alexstrasza
Characters/Major-NPCs/Alexstrasza.content:
Alexstrasza


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

The Aspect of Life, who spent years as a chained brood-mare and has not entirely recovered from it.


Red dragon (Aspect) · The Life-Binder · Red Dragonflight · Northrend / abroad
Aspect of Life, queen of the Red Dragonflight.
During The Second War the orcish Dragonmaw clan used the Demon Soul to enslave her at Grim Batol, forcing her to breed war-mounts from her own children. She was freed when the Demon Soul was destroyed.
She is the most benevolent power in the setting and the most damaged. Red dragons in mortal guise are among the few reliably good dragons a party may meet.
Related
The Dragon Aspects · Grim Batol · Demon Soul · Deathwing · The Second War · Dragons

Characters/Major-NPCs/Archimonde.title: Archimonde
Characters/Major-NPCs/Archimonde.content:
Archimonde


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

The Legion’s field commander, who destroyed Dalaran on his way to Hyjal and did not arrive.


Eredar warlock and one of Sargeras’s two chief lieutenants. Summoned to Azeroth by Kel’Thuzad using the defiled Sunwell during The Third War.
He destroyed Dalaran, then marched on Mount Hyjal to consume the Well of Eternity and remake himself as a god.


                  
                  He was destroyed 
                  
                

At the summit, Nordrassil’s power was detonated as he reached it. He was unmade utterly.
The fel residue of his death poisoned the forest below, which is now Felwood.


Related
The Burning Legion · Mount Hyjal · The Third War · Kel’Thuzad · Dalaran · Felwood · Sargeras · Nordrassil

Characters/Major-NPCs/Arthas-Menethil.title: Arthas Menethil
Characters/Major-NPCs/Arthas-Menethil.content:
Arthas Menethil


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A memory everybody at the table has. The best of them, who did the worst thing.


Human (dead) — now the Lich King · Prince of Lordaeron; the Betrayer · Scourge · (became The Lich King)
Crown Prince of Lordaeron. Paladin of the Order of the Silver Hand. Uther the Lightbringer’s student and Jaina Proudmoore’s partner.
He culled Stratholme to stop the plague, disbanded the Silver Hand when Uther refused to help, sailed to Northrend, took up Frostmourne, and lost his soul to it.
He murdered his father. He destroyed Quel’Thalas and defiled the Sunwell. He raised Kel’Thuzad. He killed Uther. He then merged with Ner’zhul to become The Lich King.


                  
                  Four years ago 
                  
                

Everyone at the table over the age of ten remembers Arthas as a hero. That’s the horror.


Related
The Lich King · The Third War · Uther the Lightbringer · Jaina Proudmoore · Stratholme · Order of the Silver Hand · Sylvanas Windrunner · Scourge

Characters/Major-NPCs/Cairne-Bloodhoof.title: Cairne Bloodhoof
Characters/Major-NPCs/Cairne-Bloodhoof.content:
Cairne Bloodhoof


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

An enormous, grey-muzzled tauren who takes a long time to answer and is worth waiting for.


Tauren · High Chieftain of the Tauren · Horde · Thunder Bluff
High Chieftain of the Tauren and Thrall’s closest advisor and elder.
He united the tauren, drove the Centaur from Mulgore with orcish help, and founded Thunder Bluff.
Related
Tauren · Thunder Bluff · Thrall · The Horde · Magatha Grimtotem · Cenarion Circle · Mulgore

Characters/Major-NPCs/Cenarius.title: Cenarius
Characters/Major-NPCs/Cenarius.content:
Cenarius


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

The forest’s own son, killed by the people he’d spent an age protecting it from.


Demigod · Lord of the Forest — dead · None · (slain in Ashenvale)
Demigod of nature, son of Elune, and the teacher of the first druids — Malfurion Stormrage and, later, the Tauren.
He was killed during The Third War by Grom Hellscream and the Warsong orcs, under the influence of Mannoroth’s blood.


                  
                  An unhealed wound 
                  
                

This is one of the ugliest things in Horde history and the Night Elves have not forgiven it. Keeper Remulos, his son, presides at Moonglade. His other son Zaetar fathered the Centaur and died for it.


Related
Cenarion Circle · Malfurion Stormrage · Grom Hellscream · Moonglade · Ashenvale · Centaur · Maraudon · Night Elves

Characters/Major-NPCs/Daelin-Proudmoore.title: Daelin Proudmoore
Characters/Major-NPCs/Daelin-Proudmoore.content:
Daelin Proudmoore


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

An admiral who could not accept that the war was over, and died proving it to his daughter.


Lord Admiral of Kul Tiras and a hero of The Second War — and Jaina Proudmoore’s father.
Three years ago he brought the Kul Tiran fleet to Kalimdor and attacked the Horde, intending to exterminate the orcs. He believed, sincerely, that his daughter had been deceived.
Related
Jaina Proudmoore · Theramore Isle · Thrall · The Four Years After · The Second War · The Alliance

Characters/Major-NPCs/Dagran-Thaurissan.content:
Dagran Thaurissan


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A crowned dwarf on an obsidian throne with a human-sized woman beside him who is not a prisoner.


Dark Iron dwarf · Emperor of the Dark Iron · Dark Iron · Blackrock Depths
Emperor of the Dark Iron Dwarves, ruling from the Imperial Seat in Blackrock Depths in Ragnaros’s shadow.

Characters/Major-NPCs/Deathwing.title: Deathwing
Characters/Major-NPCs/Deathwing.content:
Deathwing


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

An absence shaped like a catastrophe. Everyone assumes he’s dead. Nobody has a body.


Black dragon (Aspect) · The Destroyer — missing · Black Dragonflight · Unknown
Neltharion the Earth-Warder, one of the five Dragon Aspects, corrupted by The Old Gods into Deathwing the Destroyer.
He forged the Demon Soul, drained the other four flights during The War of the Ancients, and has been the black dragonflight’s ruin ever since. He was driven off at Grim Batol and has not been seen since.
Related
The Dragon Aspects · Onyxia · Nefarian · Black Dragonflight · The Old Gods · Grim Batol · The War of the Ancients

Characters/Major-NPCs/Edwin-VanCleef.title: Edwin VanCleef
Characters/Major-NPCs/Edwin-VanCleef.content:
Edwin VanCleef


                  
                  First Impression 
                  
                

A man in a red bandana on the deck of an unfinished warship, a mile underground, who does not raise his voice and does not need to.


Human · Leader of the Defias Brotherhood · Defias · The Deadmines, Westfall
Master of the Stonemasons’ Guild. He and his people rebuilt Stormwind City from rubble after The First War — walls, cathedral, keep — and when the work was done, the nobility refused to pay.
He protested. It turned violent. The masons were driven out.
He is now the most wanted man in the kingdom, holds most of Westfall, and is building a battleship in a cavern with goblin help, which he intends to sail into Stormwind Harbor.
What They Want

To be paid — literally, and he has the original contract
Stormwind’s nobility to face consequences
His people fed, which the crown will not do
To be heard, which is what he wanted before any of this

Voice

Speech: controlled, articulate, a craftsman’s precision
Tic: he talks about the work — the stone, the joins, the years
Never says: anything self-pitying
“None of you are safe.” — not a threat. A statement about the world.

Related
Defias Brotherhood · The Deadmines · Westfall · Onyxia · Kingdom of Stormwind · Stormwind City · The Interbellum

Characters/Major-NPCs/Fandral-Staghelm.title: Fandral Staghelm
Characters/Major-NPCs/Fandral-Staghelm.content:
Fandral Staghelm


                  
                  First Impression 
                  
                

An immaculate night elf with antlers and a very short supply of patience, who answers questions before you finish asking them.


Night elf · Arch Druid of the Cenarion Circle · Alliance / Cenarion Circle · Darnassus
Acting head of the Cenarion Circle while Malfurion Stormrage is lost in The Emerald Dream.
He is not a straightforward traitor at launch. He is a grieving, arrogant, competent man in a job he should not have, making a series of individually justifiable decisions that add up to catastrophe.
What They Want

Night elf immortality restored — this is genuine and it is his whole life
The Cenarion Circle led properly, meaning by him
Valstann’s death to have been worth something
Malfurion to stay exactly where he is, which he would never admit

Voice

Speech: clipped, imperious, faintly contemptuous
Tic: he finishes other people’s sentences incorrectly and moves on
Never says: his son’s name
On Teldrassil: immediate, disproportionate defensiveness

Related
Cenarion Circle · Teldrassil · Malfurion Stormrage · Darnassus · Night Elves · The War of the Shifting Sands · The Emerald Dream · Moonglade · Tyrande Whisperwind

Characters/Major-NPCs/Gelbin-Mekkatorque.title: Gelbin Mekkatorque
Characters/Major-NPCs/Gelbin-Mekkatorque.content:
Gelbin Mekkatorque


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A gnome in an oil-stained coat who runs a government out of a workshop and has not taken a day off in four years.


Gnome · High Tinker of the Gnomeregan Exiles · Alliance · Tinker Town, Ironforge
Leader of the Gnomeregan Exiles.
Related
Gnomeregan Exiles · Gnomeregan · Sicco Thermaplugg · Gnomes · Ironforge

Characters/Major-NPCs/Grom-Hellscream.title: Grom Hellscream
Characters/Major-NPCs/Grom-Hellscream.content:
Grom Hellscream


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

The orc who drank the blood twice: once to damn his people, and once to free them.


Orc · Chieftain of the Warsong — dead · Horde · Demon Fall Canyon, Ashenvale
Chieftain of the Warsong clan. The first orc to drink Mannoroth’s blood, damning his entire race to the demonic curse.
At Demon Fall Canyon in Ashenvale, he drank it one final time to gain the strength to kill Mannoroth — and in doing so, broke the blood curse forever. He died in Thrall’s arms.
Orc skin has been fading from red toward brown ever since. Children born after are the first free generation in living memory.


                  
                  Sacred ground 
                  
                

Demon Fall Canyon is orcish holy ground and it is in night elf territory. Neither side has worked out how to handle that.


Related
Orcs · Mannoroth · Thrall · Ashenvale · The Third War · The Burning Legion · Orgrimmar

Characters/Major-NPCs/Gul'dan.title: Gul'dan
Characters/Major-NPCs/Gul'dan.content:
Gul’dan


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

The orc who sold his people to demons for power and then complained that the price was high.


The first orcish warlock, apprenticed to Ner’zhul and recruited by Kil’jaeden. He founded the Shadow Council, fed the clans Mannoroth’s blood, and — working with the possessed Medivh — opened the Dark Portal.
He was killed by demons while trying to claim the Tomb of Sargeras for himself during The Second War. His skull became a Legion artifact and was eventually consumed by Illidan Stormrage.


                  
                  The orcs' scapegoat and their explanation 
                  
                

Every orc knows Gul’dan’s name. He is the reason the Horde’s crimes were not entirely the Horde’s fault — and orcs are very tired of having to explain that to people.


Related
Orcs · Shadow Council · Mannoroth · Medivh · Dark Portal · The First War · Kil’jaeden · Illidan Stormrage

Characters/Major-NPCs/Illidan-Stormrage.title: Illidan Stormrage
Characters/Major-NPCs/Illidan-Stormrage.content:
Illidan Stormrage


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

The Betrayer. Blindfolded, tattooed, winged, and in Outland — which is to say, someone else’s problem.


Malfurion Stormrage’s twin. Jealous of his brother, in love with Tyrande Whisperwind, and unwilling to live in a world without magic.
He betrayed the resistance to Sargeras during The War of the Ancients and was given his demonic sight. After The Sundering he secretly created a second Well of Eternity on Mount Hyjal, and Malfurion imprisoned him for ten thousand years.
Released during The Third War, he consumed the Skull of Gul’dan, became part-demon, and fled to Outland, where he now rules with Kael’thas Sunstrider and Lady Vashj.
Related
Malfurion Stormrage · Tyrande Whisperwind · The War of the Ancients · The Sundering · Mount Hyjal · Kael’thas Sunstrider · Lady Vashj · The Twisting Nether

Characters/Major-NPCs/Jaina-Proudmoore.title: Jaina Proudmoore
Characters/Major-NPCs/Jaina-Proudmoore.content:
Jaina Proudmoore


                  
                  First Impression 
                  
                

A young blonde woman in blue robes who looks tired in a way that has nothing to do with sleep, and who is unfailingly, exhaustingly polite.


Human · Ruler of Theramore; archmage · Theramore (Alliance) · Theramore Isle
The most powerful human mage alive and the Kirin Tor’s most prominent living member. She was Arthas Menethil’s partner before The Third War, and she left him at Stratholme when he culled the city.
Warned by Medivh, she led the human exodus to Kalimdor and founded Theramore Isle — and made peace with Thrall at Mount Hyjal, which is why the world still exists.
What They Want

The peace to hold — she has already paid everything for it
Theramore to survive as proof that coexistence is possible
Her father’s death to have meant something
Not to have been wrong about Arthas

Voice

Speech: careful, diplomatic, over-considered
Tic: she apologizes for things that are not her fault
Never says: Arthas’s name if she can avoid it
Under pressure: she is an archmage and she stops being polite

Related
Theramore · Theramore Isle · Thrall · Arthas Menethil · Daelin Proudmoore · Kirin Tor · Dustwallow Marsh · The Third War

Characters/Major-NPCs/Kael'thas-Sunstrid.title: Kael'thas Sunstrider
Characters/Major-NPCs/Kael'thas-Sunstrid.content:
Kael’thas Sunstrider


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

The last prince of a dead kingdom, who renamed his people after their dead and led them somewhere nobody can follow.


Prince of Quel’Thalas, son of King Anasterian, and a Kirin Tor archmage.
When Arthas Menethil destroyed his kingdom and defiled the Sunwell, Kael’thas renamed the survivors sin’dorei — Blood Elves, children of blood — and led them in search of a cure for their arcane withdrawal.
He took them through the Dark Portal into Outland and fell in with Illidan Stormrage.

Blood Elves · Quel’Thalas · High Elves · Illidan Stormrage · Dark Portal · Kirin Tor · Arthas Menethil · Lady Vashj

Characters/Major-NPCs/Kel'Thuzad.title: Kel'Thuzad
Characters/Major-NPCs/Kel'Thuzad.content:
Kel’Thuzad


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A robed skeleton wreathed in cold, who was a Kirin Tor archmage and chose this.


Lich · Archlich of the Scourge · Scourge · Northrend / Naxxramas
A Kirin Tor archmage who left the order voluntarily to serve The Lich King. He founded the Cult of the Damned, engineered the plague of undeath that destroyed Lordaeron, and was killed and then raised as a lich using the defiled Sunwell.
He summoned Archimonde to Azeroth.
Related
Scourge · The Lich King · Naxxramas · Kirin Tor · The Third War · Scholomance · Arthas Menethil

Characters/Major-NPCs/Khadgar.title: Khadgar
Characters/Major-NPCs/Khadgar.content:
Khadgar


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

The apprentice who killed his own master, aged sixty years in an afternoon, and is now stranded in another world.


Medivh’s apprentice, who helped kill him at Karazhan in Year 3 and was aged to an old man by the act.
He served with distinction through The Second War and destroyed the Dark Portal at its close. During The Invasion of Draenor he sealed the portal from the far side to stop Ner’zhul’s rifts — stranding himself and the entire Alliance Expedition.


                  
                  Missing, presumed dead 
                  
                

Khadgar, Turalyon, Alleria Windrunner, Danath Trollbane, and Kurdran Wildhammer have been unaccounted for since Year 18. Their families have not given up. Nobody has any evidence either way.
That’s a genuine open mystery at launch and it costs nothing to use.


Related
Medivh · Karazhan · Dark Portal · The Second War · The Invasion of Draenor · Kirin Tor · Ner’zhul

Characters/Major-NPCs/Kil'jaeden.title: Kil'jaeden
Characters/Major-NPCs/Kil'jaeden.content:
Kil’jaeden


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

The Legion’s other lieutenant, still alive, still out there, and the one who built the Lich King.


Eredar, one of Sargeras’s two chief lieutenants, and the architect of the Legion’s Azeroth campaign.
He corrupted the Orcs through Gul’dan and the blood of Mannoroth. He captured Ner’zhul after Draenor’s destruction, flayed his spirit, and remade him as The Lich King to prepare Azeroth for invasion.
Related
The Burning Legion · The Lich King · Ner’zhul · Gul’dan · Orcs · Sargeras · Jaedenar · The Twisting Nether

Characters/Major-NPCs/Lady-Vashj.title: Lady Vashj
Characters/Major-NPCs/Lady-Vashj.content:
Lady Vashj


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

Azshara’s handmaiden, ten thousand years underwater, now serving a different master in a different world.


One of Queen Azshara’s original Highborne handmaidens, transformed into a Naga during The Sundering.
During The Third War she allied with Illidan Stormrage and took a large naga contingent to Outland with him.


                  
                  Which raises a question 
                  
                

Naga are appearing on Azeroth’s coasts in increasing numbers — Darkshore, Queen Azshara, Desolace, Stranglethorn Vale. If Vashj took the loyal ones to Outland, whose orders are these ones following?


Related
Naga · Queen Azshara · Illidan Stormrage · The Sundering · The Twisting Nether · Darkshore

Characters/Major-NPCs/Magatha-Grimtotem.title: Magatha Grimtotem
Characters/Major-NPCs/Magatha-Grimtotem.content:
Magatha Grimtotem


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

An elderly tauren shaman who is unfailingly respectful to Cairne Bloodhoof’s face and has never once meant it.


Tauren · Matriarch of the Grimtotem · Horde (nominally) · Thunder Bluff / Kalimdor-wide
Matriarch of the Grimtotem tribe, scattered across Feralas, Stonetalon Mountains, Thousand Needles, Desolace, and Dustwallow Marsh.
She believes Cairne Bloodhoof sold the Tauren to the orcs for nothing, that the Horde is a leash, and that the tauren should be ruled by strength — hers.
She operates openly at Thunder Bluff as an elder, which is either Cairne’s greatest kindness or his greatest mistake.
Related
Tauren · Cairne Bloodhoof · Thunder Bluff · The Horde · Feralas · Thousand Needles

Characters/Major-NPCs/Magni-Bronzebeard.content:
Magni Bronzebeard


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A broad dwarf with a beard past his belt and a hammer he still uses, who is sitting on two pieces of news he cannot bring himself to share.


Dwarf · King of Ironforge · Alliance · Ironforge
King of Ironforge and the Alliance’s most reliable partner.

Characters/Major-NPCs/Malfurion-Stormrag.title: Malfurion Stormrage
Characters/Major-NPCs/Malfurion-Stormrag.content:
Malfurion Stormrage


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A sleeping body in a barrow den that has not moved in four years, and a spirit somewhere that cannot be reached.


Night elf · Arch Druid — lost in the Dream · Alliance / Cenarion Circle · Moonglade (body) / The Emerald Dream (spirit)
The first druid, taught by Cenarius. He defeated Sargeras’s incursion in The War of the Ancients, imprisoned his own brother Illidan, and founded the Cenarion Circle.
He entered The Emerald Dream to investigate the corruption spreading through it, and has not come back. His body sleeps in the Stormrage Barrow Dens at Moonglade.

The Emerald Dream · Cenarion Circle · Fandral Staghelm · Tyrande Whisperwind · Moonglade · Ysera · Cenarius · Illidan Stormrage

Characters/Major-NPCs/Malygos.title: Malygos
Characters/Major-NPCs/Malygos.content:
Malygos


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

The Aspect of Magic, who watched Deathwing murder almost his entire flight and has not been coherent since.


Blue dragon (Aspect) · The Spell-Weaver — insane · Blue Dragonflight · The Nexus, Northrend
Aspect of Magic. Deathwing used the Demon Soul to annihilate nearly the entire Blue Dragonflight during The War of the Ancients, and Malygos has been insane for ten thousand years.
Related
The Dragon Aspects · Blue Dragonflight · Deathwing · Arcane Magic and the Well of Eternity · Winterspring · Kirin Tor

Characters/Major-NPCs/Mannoroth.title: Mannoroth
Characters/Major-NPCs/Mannoroth.content:
Mannoroth


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

The pit lord whose blood damned an entire species, killed by the first orc who drank it.


The pit lord whose blood Gul’dan fed to the orcish clans on Draenor, binding them to the Burning Legion and turning a shamanic people into an army. Their skin turned red. Their rage became permanent.
Grom Hellscream was the first to drink it.


                  
                  And the last 
                  
                

At Demon Fall Canyon in Ashenvale, Grom drank demon blood one final time to gain the strength to kill Mannoroth — and in doing so broke the blood curse forever. He died in Thrall’s arms.
Orc skin has been fading toward brown ever since. Children born after are the first free generation in living memory.


Related
Orcs · Grom Hellscream · Gul’dan · The Burning Legion · Ashenvale · Thrall · The Third War

Characters/Major-NPCs/Medivh.title: Medivh
Characters/Major-NPCs/Medivh.content:
Medivh


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A dead man who has been seen since, giving good advice, and nobody can explain it.


Human · The last Guardian of Tirisfal — dead, mostly · None · Karazhan, Deadwind Pass
The last Guardian of Tirisfal. Son of Aegwynn, and possessed by Sargeras from birth.
Under that possession he contacted Gul’dan and opened the Dark Portal, starting The First War. He was killed at Karazhan in Year 3 by Anduin Lothar, Khadgar, and Garona.
Related
Guardians of Tirisfal · Karazhan · Aegwynn · Sargeras · Dark Portal · The First War · Deadwind Pass · Jaina Proudmoore

Characters/Major-NPCs/Ner'zhul.title: Ner'zhul
Characters/Major-NPCs/Ner'zhul.content:
Ner’zhul


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

An orc shaman who was tricked, then repented, then tore his own world apart, then was flayed into a weapon.


Elder shaman of the orcish Shadowmoon clan and Gul’dan’s teacher. He was the first to be contacted by Kil’jaeden and the first to realize it was a trap — but Gul’dan had already taken over.
After The Second War he reopened the Dark Portal and tore open so many rifts that Draenor shattered into Outland (The Invasion of Draenor).
Related
The Lich King · Arthas Menethil · Kil’jaeden · Gul’dan · The Invasion of Draenor · Scourge · Northrend

Characters/Major-NPCs/Orgrim-Doomhammer.title: Orgrim Doomhammer
Characters/Major-NPCs/Orgrim-Doomhammer.content:
Orgrim Doomhammer


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

The Warchief who killed his own predecessor for selling the orcs to demons, and lost the war anyway.


Warchief of the Horde during The Second War. He killed Warchief Blackhand — Rend Blackhand’s father — on discovering that Gul’dan and the Shadow Council were the Horde’s real masters, and executed the Council.
He led the Horde to the gates of Lordaeron and was broken at Blackrock Spire. He spent the internment years free and in hiding.
He died fighting beside Thrall in the campaign that founded the New Horde, and gave him the Doomhammer, which Thrall carries still.
Related
Thrall · The Second War · Gul’dan · Shadow Council · Orcs · Rend Blackhand · Doomhammer

Characters/Major-NPCs/Queen-Azshara.title: Queen Azshara
Characters/Major-NPCs/Queen-Azshara.content:
Queen Azshara


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

The most beautiful queen who ever lived, who agreed to unmake the world for a promotion, and has been at the bottom of the sea ever since.


Queen of the Kaldorei empire at its height, and its destroyer. Addicted to the Well of Eternity, she and her Highborne contacted Sargeras and began widening a portal to let the Burning Legion in — in exchange for godhood.
The War of the Ancients and The Sundering followed. Her palace sank.
Related
Azshara (the zone) · Naga · The War of the Ancients · The Sundering · Sargeras · Night Elves · Lady Vashj · The Old Gods · Arcane Magic and the Well of Eternity

Characters/Major-NPCs/Ragnaros.title: Ragnaros
Characters/Major-NPCs/Ragnaros.content:
Ragnaros


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A being of living magma the size of a building, rising out of a lake of fire, and profoundly annoyed to have been woken.


Fire elemental lord · The Firelord · Elemental / Dark Iron · Molten Core
Elemental Lord of Fire. Summoned by the Dark Iron Dwarves during the War of the Three Hammers to win their civil war. He came, destroyed their city, raised Blackrock Mountain in the process, and enslaved them.
He is bound in Molten Core. The Dark Iron are working to widen that binding. Nobody has reached him.
Related
Molten Core · Dark Iron Dwarves · Blackrock Mountain · The Elemental Planes · Hydraxian Waterlords · Dagran Thaurissan

Characters/Major-NPCs/Rend-Blackhand.title: Rend Blackhand
Characters/Major-NPCs/Rend-Blackhand.content:
Rend Blackhand


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A red-skinned orc on a throne, still wearing the trappings of a Horde that lost thirty years ago, being handled by his own advisor.


Orc · Self-styled Warchief of the Dark Horde · Dark Horde · Upper Blackrock Spire
Son of Warchief Blackhand, who led the Horde in The First War. Rend rejected Thrall’s New Horde entirely, kept his fel corruption, and holds Blackrock Spire with the Dark Horde.
He styles himself Warchief. He rides the chromatic drake Gyth.
Related
Dark Horde · Nefarian · Upper Blackrock Spire · Blackrock Mountain · Thrall · Orcs · Burning Steppes

Characters/Major-NPCs/Sargeras.title: Sargeras
Characters/Major-NPCs/Sargeras.content:
Sargeras


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A titan who looked at creation, decided it was irredeemable, and has spent an age trying to finish the job.


Once the Pantheon’s champion — the titan charged with hunting demons across the cosmos. He concluded that all life was inevitably corruptible and that the only mercy was erasure, freed the demons he had imprisoned, and founded the Burning Legion.
His Reach Into Azeroth

He tempted Queen Azshara and the Highborne, starting The War of the Ancients
Aegwynn destroyed his avatar in Northrend — and he hid inside her, passing to her son

Sicco Thermaplugg

A gnome in a ruined throne room surrounded by bomb dispensers, entirely delighted with how things turned out.


Gnome · Mad ruler of Gnomeregan · None · Gnomeregan
Advisor to Gelbin Mekkatorque, and the architect of the worst atrocity in gnomish history.
He recommended flooding Gnomeregan with radiation to purge invading troggs. Mekkatorque agreed. It killed eighty percent of the gnomes and none of the troggs.

Characters/Major-NPCs/Sylvanas-Windrunne.title: Sylvanas Windrunner
Characters/Major-NPCs/Sylvanas-Windrunne.content:
Sylvanas Windrunner


                  
                  First Impression 
                  
                

A pale ranger-general in dark leather, bow across her back, who speaks quietly and does not blink as often as a living person would.


Undead high elf (banshee) · Banshee Queen of the Forsaken · Horde (Forsaken) · Undercity
Ranger-General of Quel’Thalas. She died defending it from Arthas Menethil, who raised her as a banshee and made her hunt her own people — deliberately, as a punishment for the trouble she’d caused him.
When his grip weakened after The Third War, she tore free, took a large portion of the undead with her, and named them the Forsaken.
She built Undercity beneath the ruins of Lordaeron’s throne room, where Arthas murdered his father, and she makes every visitor walk through it.
What They Want

Arthas Menethil destroyed — personally, and slowly
A homeland the Forsaken cannot be evicted from
The Horde’s protection for exactly as long as it is useful
Never to be controlled by anything again

Voice

Speech: quiet, clipped, with an elven cadence underneath
Tic: she does not raise her voice. Ever. It’s more frightening.
Never says: anything about her sisters, Alleria and Vereesa
“Dark Lady watch over you.” — her people’s benediction, and she permits it

Characters/Major-NPCs/Thrall.title: Thrall
Characters/Major-NPCs/Thrall.content:
Thrall


                  
                  First Impression 
                  
                

A very large orc in plain mail who listens for a long time before speaking, and whose accent is a human nobleman’s — because that’s who raised him.


Orc · Warchief of the Horde · Horde · Orgrimmar
Born in an internment camp. Raised by Aedelas Blackmoore at Durnholde Keep as a gladiator and a strategic asset — taught to read, to fight, and to know his place. He escaped at twenty, found the Frostwolf clan and the shaman Drek’Thar, and became the first orc in three generations to touch the elements.
He freed the camps, liberated Grom Hellscream, inherited Orgrim Doomhammer’s hammer, and led his people west to a land nobody else wanted.


                  
                  The literate warchief 
                  
                

Thrall reads. He quotes human philosophy. He negotiates. Orcish traditionalists find this deeply suspicious and he knows it and does it anyway.


What They Want

A homeland that cannot be taken away
Peace with the Alliance — genuinely, not tactically
To prove the orcs are not what they were made into
To not become Blackmoore, which is a fear he has never spoken aloud

Voice

Speech: measured, formal, faintly human-educated
Tic: long pauses before answering — he is actually thinking, not posturing
Never says: anything he hasn’t decided he means
“Lok’tar ogar.” — used sparingly, and it lands when he does

Characters/Major-NPCs/Tirion-Fordring.content:
Tirion Fordring


                  
                  First Impression 
                  
                

An old man in a farmer’s coat outside a one-room hut, splitting wood. There is a warhorse in the paddock that is much too good for a farmer.


Human · Disgraced paladin; hermit · None · Eastern Plaguelands
One of the five founding knights of the Order of the Silver Hand. He was excommunicated and exiled years ago for a single act: he spared the life of an orc, Eitrigg, who had saved his — and refused to recant.
He lost his lands, his title, his order, and access to his son.
He now lives alone in a hut in the Eastern Plaguelands, drinking, surrounded by the Scourge, and refusing to be the man everyone needs him to be.
What They Want

To be left alone — he says this, and it isn’t true
His son out of the Scarlet Crusade, alive
The Silver Hand to have meant what he thought it meant
To stop being angry, which he has not managed

Voice

Speech: blunt, tired, occasionally very funny
Tic: he deflects sincerity with sarcasm and it fools nobody
Never says: Uther’s name without pausing first
When it matters: the paladin is still entirely there, and it is startling

Not a government. A treaty organization between:

Gilneas walled itself off. Kul Tiras has withdrawn in fury since Daelin Proudmoore’s death. Stromgarde is a ruin. Alterac was dissolved for treason. The High Elves left after the Second War and have never come back.
The Alliance of Lordaeron was seven kingdoms. This is four and a half.

“The Light, the crown, and the common defense.” In practice: humans provide legitimacy, dwarves provide industry, gnomes provide engineering, and night elves provide the thing nobody says out loud — they lost their immortality saving a world that mostly didn’t notice, and they are owed.

Lore/Cosmology/Arcane-Magic-and-the-Well.title: Arcane Magic and the Well of Eternity
Lore/Cosmology/Arcane-Magic-and-the-Well.content:
Arcane Magic and the Well of Eternity
The Well
A lake of pure, raw magic at the heart of ancient Kalimdor — created when the Titans drained the world’s chaotic energies into a single reservoir. Everything arcane on Azeroth traces back to it.
The Kaldorei built their civilization on its shores and grew powerful, beautiful, and immortal. Queen Azshara and her Highborne grew addicted to it, and their reckless spellwork drew the attention of Sargeras — leading directly to The War of the Ancients and The Sundering, which tore the continent apart and left the Well’s site as the Maelstrom.
The Second Well
Illidan Stormrage, unwilling to live in a world without magic, poured stolen vials of the Well’s water into a lake atop Mount Hyjal, creating a second Well. His brother Malfurion Stormrage imprisoned him for ten thousand years for it. The Dragon Aspects grew Nordrassil, the World Tree, over it — binding the night elves’ immortality to it.
The Sunwell
High elf exiles, banished for practicing arcane magic, founded Quel’Thalas and created the Sunwell from a stolen vial. It sustained them for millennia.
Arcane Magic in the World

Kirin Tor — the mage-rulers of Dalaran, now homeless
Malygos, Aspect of Magic, has been insane since the Sundering — nobody is minding the store
Arcane magic is an addiction. Every elven civilization that touched it has fallen.
It is also a beacon. Heavy arcane use attracts the Burning Legion. This is precisely how the Legion found Azeroth the first time.

Related

The Sisters of Elune are her priesthood, headed by Tyrande Whisperwind at the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. Moonwells — pools of Elune’s blessing — are found across kaldorei territory.


                  
                  Contrast with the Light 
                  
                

The Holy Light is a philosophy that happens to work. Elune is a goddess who is petitioned. Night elf faith is devotional and personal in a way human Light-worship isn’t, and priests of both would find the other’s practice strange.


Tauren identify Elune with Mu’sha, one of the Earthmother’s eyes — a rare piece of genuine cross-cultural theology, and a nice detail to give a tauren and night elf druid to argue about.

The Earth-Warder listened to whispers from beneath the world — The Old Gods — and forged the Demon Soul, a disc into which the other four flights unknowingly poured their power. He used it to shatter them, and the dragons have never recovered. He is Deathwing now.

The Elemental Planes

The Four Lords

He is the campaign’s most immediate elemental threat.Neptulon the TidehunterWaterThe Abyssal MawDistant. The Hydraxian Waterlords serve him and oppose Ragnaros.Therazane the StonemotherEarthDeepholmBarely referenced in 2004Al’Akir the WindlordAirThe SkywallBarely referenced in 2004
Shamanism


                  
                  Petition, not command 
                  
                

Orcs, Tauren, and Darkspear Trolls practice shamanism — a negotiated relationship. Elementals are not summoned; they are asked, and they can refuse. Thrall rebuilt orcish shamanism from Drek’Thar’s teaching after generations of fel corruption severed the orcs from it entirely.
The Alliance has no equivalent tradition at launch. This is why shaman is Horde-locked, and it is good lore rather than arbitrary balance.


Ragnaros and the Dark Iron
The Dark Iron Dwarves summoned Ragnaros during the War of the Three Hammers. He came, obliterated their city, and made them his slaves — a bargain they still consider to have gone well. He is bound in Molten Core beneath Blackrock Mountain, and Emperor Dagran Thaurissan rules in his shadow.

Lore/Cosmology/The-Emerald-Dream.title: The Emerald Dream
Lore/Cosmology/The-Emerald-Dream.content:
The Emerald Dream
Azeroth as it would have been if no thinking creature had ever touched it. A vast, verdant mirror-world overlaid on the waking one, shaped by Ysera and the Green Dragonflight, and the source of all druidic power.
How It Works

Druids enter through the Emerald Enchantment — a sleep that can last centuries
The Cenarion Circle maintains Barrow Dens at Moonglade and Teldrassil where sleepers’ bodies lie
Time runs strangely. A night elf may sleep a thousand years and wake having missed everything.
Green dragons guard the portals — Ashenvale, Feralas, the Hinterlands, Duskwood

The Problem
Malfurion
Malfurion Stormrage, the first druid and the Alliance’s greatest asset, is in there. His body sleeps; his spirit is trapped. Tyrande Whisperwind has been waiting four years. Fandral Staghelm presides over the Cenarion Circle in his absence, and does not seem in a hurry to get him back.

Lore/Cosmology/The-Holy-Light.title: The Holy Light
Lore/Cosmology/The-Holy-Light.content:
The Holy Light
Not a god. A philosophy — and one that, inexplicably and reliably, works.
The Three Virtues

Respect — all things have worth
Tenacity — persist despite adversity
Compassion — the two above, turned outward

The Church of the Holy Light teaches that by holding these truths, a person aligns themselves with the fundamental benevolence of creation, and creation answers. It heals. It burns undead. It has never once explained itself.
Institutions

The Church of the Holy Light — Stormwind Cathedral, Northshire Abbey, the human heartland
The Order of the Silver Hand — the paladin order founded by Uther the Lightbringer in the Second War. Shattered. Arthas disbanded it; Uther is dead; its survivors are scattered between the Argent Dawn and the Scarlet Crusade.
Dwarven faith — Ironforge adopted the Light through Alliance contact; Dwarves make devout, pragmatic paladins

The Shadow
The Light’s opposite is not evil — it is the Void, drawn on by shadow priests and warlocks. Forsaken and troll priests wield it openly. Human priests are taught both and warned about one.


                  
                  The Forsaken problem 
                  
                

Forsaken priests can channel the Light, and it hurts them to do it. Undead flesh recoils from it. A Forsaken priest who heals an ally is choosing agony. This is excellent characterization and worth surfacing.


The Crisis at Launch

Lore/Cosmology/The-Titans.title: The Titans
Lore/Cosmology/The-Titans.content:
The Titans


                  
                  What the Explorers' League will tell you 
                  
                

“Everything you’re standing on was built, lad. Every mountain’s a decision. Somebody drew a plan.”


Colossal beings of living metal and unimaginable power who came to Azeroth in the world’s first age, found it a churning chaos ruled by The Old Gods, and ordered it.
What They Did

Waged war on the Old Gods and their elemental lieutenants, and won
Chained the Old Gods deep beneath the earth rather than kill them — killing them would have destroyed the world
Banished the Elemental Lords to The Elemental Planes
Raised mountains, carved seas, and seeded life
Created the titan-forged: Earthen (who became Dwarves), giants, mechagnomes (who became Gnomes), and the vrykul
Appointed the five Dragon Aspects as caretakers and departed

What They Left Behind
Their machinery is still running, unattended, all over the world:

                  The dwarven revelation 
                  
                

The Explorers’ League discovering that dwarves were made — that they are the Earthen, flesh-cursed — is one of vanilla’s genuine live storylines. It runs through Uldaman and it is unresolved at launch. Magni Bronzebeard takes it very personally.

Lore/Cosmology/The-Twisting-Nether.content:
The Twisting Nether
The chaotic void between worlds — a churning purple immaterium of raw magic where demons are born, where they return when killed, and across which the Burning Legion sails its endless crusade.
Key Facts

Demons do not truly die on Azeroth. Kill one and its essence returns to the Nether to re-form. Permanent destruction requires killing them in the Nether — which is why Illidan Stormrage and others obsess over reaching it.
Warlocks draw summoned demons through the Nether. Every summoning punches a small hole in reality.
Portals — the Dark Portal is a stable Nether-tunnel between Azeroth and Draenor
Draenor was shattered by Ner’zhul opening too many portals at once; its remnant, Outland, now hangs in the Nether

Lore/History/The-First-War.title: The First War
Lore/History/The-First-War.content:
The First War


                  
                  Years 0–5 ADP 
                  
                

The orcish Horde came through the Dark Portal into the Swamp of Sorrows and destroyed the Kingdom of Stormwind.
What Happened

Medivh, possessed by Sargeras, opens the Dark Portal in collaboration with the warlock Gul’dan.
The orcs — already corrupted by Mannoroth’s blood and dying of it on Draenor — invade a world they were promised.
King Llane Wrynn is assassinated by Garona Halforcen under Gul’dan’s compulsion.
Stormwind Keep falls. Anduin Lothar leads the human refugees by sea north to Lordaeron.

Why It Still Matters
The orcs’ arrival was never their own idea — they were a weapon, aimed by a demon-possessed human wizard. This is the single most important fact in Alliance–Horde relations and almost nobody on the Alliance side believes it. Stormwind City was rebuilt after this war, and that reconstruction creates the Defias Brotherhood.
Related
Medivh · Gul’dan · Orcs · Dark Portal · Stormwind City · The Second War

Lore/History/The-Four-Years-After.title: The Four Years After
Lore/History/The-Four-Years-After.content:
The Four Years After


                  
                  Years 25–29 ADP 
                  
                

The reconstruction. New nations built on new continents by people who had lost their old ones — and a peace that is only holding because everyone is too tired to break it.
What Happened

Durotar is claimed. Thrall settles his people on barren red rock nobody else wanted, and raises Orgrimmar.
The Tauren unite. Cairne Bloodhoof drives the centaur from Mulgore with orcish help and founds Thunder Bluff. The tauren join the Horde out of debt and conviction.
The Darkspear Trolls settle in Durotar under Vol’jin, having lost the Echo Isles to the madman Zalazane.
Teldrassil is grown. Fandral Staghelm raises a second World Tree without the Dragon Aspects’ blessing. It is already showing corruption. Darnassus is built in its branches.
The night elves join the Alliance — a decision Tyrande makes largely alone, with Malfurion lost in The Emerald Dream.
The Battle of Theramore (Yr 26). Admiral Daelin Proudmoore arrives from Kul Tiras and attacks the Horde in defiance of his daughter. Jaina Proudmoore stands aside and lets the orcs kill him to preserve the peace. She has not been forgiven by anyone.
Gnomeregan falls. Sicco Thermaplugg triggers a radiation purge that fails to kill the invading troggs and does kill most of the gnomes. Gelbin Mekkatorque leads the survivors into Ironforge.
Ragnaros is summoned. The Dark Iron Dwarves draw the Firelord into Molten Core beneath Blackrock Mountain.
The cold war calcifies. Ashenvale and Hillsbrad Foothills become permanent low-grade battlefronts.

Why It Still Matters
This is the present. Every institution the players interact with is four years old or four years broken. Nothing has settled. Nothing is traditional. Every alliance is provisional and every border is an argument.
Related
The State of the World · Timeline of Azeroth · Thrall · Jaina Proudmoore · Teldrassil · Gnomeregan · Ragnaros

Lore/History/The-Guardians-of-Tirisfal.title: The Guardians of Tirisfal
Lore/History/The-Guardians-of-Tirisfal.content:
The Guardians of Tirisfal


                  
                  ~2,600 BDP to Year 3 ADP 
                  
                

A secret order that invested the combined power of the world’s greatest mages into a single champion each generation, to fight the Burning Legion unseen. It ended in the worst possible way.
What Happened

The Council of Tirisfal is founded after the Troll Wars, drawing on human, elf, and dragon members.
Aegwynn is chosen Guardian and holds the office for nearly 900 years, defying the Council’s authority.
She destroys an avatar of Sargeras in Northrend — and entombs it, unaware that Sargeras allowed it, and that his spirit has hidden inside her.
Aegwynn conceives a son, Medivh, and passes the Guardian’s power to him at birth. Sargeras passes with it.
Medivh awakens possessed, contacts Gul’dan on Draenor, and opens the Dark Portal.
Medivh is slain at Karazhan by Anduin Lothar, Khadgar, and Garona Halforcen in Year 3.

Why It Still Matters
Every war of the last thirty years traces back to this order’s single point of failure. Karazhan stands abandoned and sealed in Deadwind Pass at launch — a tower full of a dead Guardian’s secrets that nobody has dared enter. Aegwynn is alive, in hiding, and elderly.
Related
Medivh · Aegwynn · Karazhan · The First War · Kirin Tor · Sargeras

Lore/History/The-Interbellum.title: The Interbellum
Lore/History/The-Interbellum.content:
The Interbellum


                  
                  Years 8–23 ADP 
                  
                

Fifteen years of exhausted, ugly peace. The Alliance won and did not know what to do next.
What Happened

Defeated orcs are herded into internment camps across Lordaeron, where they sink into a listless lethargy — the withdrawal of a people cut off from demonic blood.
Thrall is born in captivity and raised by Aedelas Blackmoore at Durnholde Keep as a gladiator and a tool.
The Alliance fractures. Gilneas walls itself off behind the Greymane Wall. Stromgarde and Kul Tiras drift. The high elves withdraw to Quel’Thalas.
Stormwind is rebuilt — and the Stonemasons’ Guild, who did the work, are never paid. Their leader Edwin VanCleef takes them underground as the Defias Brotherhood.
Year 20: Thrall escapes, finds the Frostwolf clan and Drek’Thar, and learns shamanism — the first orc in generations to touch the elements.
Year 21: Thrall frees the camps, liberates Grom Hellscream, and inherits the Doomhammer. The New Horde is born.

Why It Still Matters
This is where the campaign’s grudges are manufactured. The Defias, the Syndicate, Gilneas’s isolation, the high elves’ departure, and Thrall’s entire worldview all come out of these fifteen years. The Alliance’s biggest internal problems are self-inflicted debts from this period.
Related
Thrall · Defias Brotherhood · Edwin VanCleef · Orcs · Grom Hellscream · Hillsbrad Foothills

Lore/History/The-Invasion-of-Draenor.title: The Invasion of Draenor
Lore/History/The-Invasion-of-Draenor.content:
The Invasion of Draenor


                  
                  Years 17–18 ADP 
                  
                

The Alliance Expedition went back through a reopened Dark Portal to end the orcish threat at its source. Draenor did not survive.
What Happened

The shaman Ner’zhul reopens the Dark Portal to seek new worlds to conquer.
An Alliance Expedition under Turalyon and Khadgar pursues him through.
Ner’zhul opens multiple portals at once. The competing rifts tear Draenor apart.
Khadgar seals the portal from the Draenor side. The Expedition is stranded.
Ner’zhul flees into the Twisting Nether, where Kil’jaeden captures him, flays his spirit, and remakes him as The Lich King.

Why It Still Matters
Draenor’s shattered remnant becomes Outland — unreachable at launch. The Expedition (Turalyon, Alleria Windrunner, Danath Trollbane, Kurdran Wildhammer) is missing, presumed dead, which is a live mystery in 2004 and a fine plot hook. And the Lich King is created here — meaning the Second War produced the Third.
Related
Ner’zhul · The Lich King · Dark Portal · Khadgar · Blasted Lands · The Twisting Nether

Lore/History/The-Second-War.title: The Second War
Lore/History/The-Second-War.content:
The Second War


                  
                  Years 6–8 ADP 
                  
                

The Horde pushed north into Lordaeron. Seven human kingdoms, the dwarves, the gnomes, and the high elves formed the Alliance of Lordaeron and stopped them.
What Happened

Anduin Lothar unites the human kingdoms under King Terenas Menethil. Ironforge, Gnomeregan, and Quel’Thalas join.
The Horde, now led by Orgrim Doomhammer, enslaves the Red Dragonflight using the Demon Soul — Alexstrasza is chained in Grim Batol.
Lord Perenolde of Alterac betrays the Alliance, opening a pass to the Horde. Alterac is later dissolved in disgrace.
Quel’Thalas is burned. The high elves never forgive the Alliance’s slow response.
Uther the Lightbringer founds the Order of the Silver Hand — the first paladins.
Lothar dies at Blackrock Spire. Turalyon takes command and breaks the Horde.
Khadgar destroys the Dark Portal.

Why It Still Matters
Alterac’s treason creates the Syndicate. The enslaved dragons create the Dragonmaw and the mystery of Grim Batol. The high elves’ bitterness leads most of them to leave the Alliance. And the surviving orcs are put in internment camps — where Thrall is born.
Related
The Interbellum · Orgrim Doomhammer · Uther the Lightbringer · Alterac Mountains · Syndicate · Grim Batol · Alexstrasza

Lore/History/The-Sundering.title: The Sundering
Lore/History/The-Sundering.content:
The Sundering


                  
                  ~10,000 years before the Dark Portal 
                  
                

The Well of Eternity collapsed in on itself and took the continent with it. A single landmass became the world we know.
What Happened

The Well implodes. The resulting cataclysm shatters Kalimdor into the continents of today.
Eighty percent of the night elf population dies. The site of the Well becomes the Maelstrom.
Queen Azshara and her drowned court are transformed by an Old God’s bargain into the Naga.
Illidan Stormrage secretly poured stolen Well-water onto Mount Hyjal, creating a second Well. Malfurion imprisons him beneath Hyjal for ten thousand years.
The Dragon Aspects grow Nordrassil, the first World Tree, over the new Well — granting the night elves immortality and a duty to guard it.

Why It Still Matters
The geography of the entire campaign is Sundering debris. So is night elf immortality — which was spent at Mount Hyjal four years ago, meaning every night elf PC is experiencing mortality for the first time in ten millennia. That is not a footnote. That is a personality.
Related
The War of the Ancients · Nordrassil · Naga · Illidan Stormrage · Night Elves · Queen Azshara

Lore/History/The-Third-War.title: The Third War
Lore/History/The-Third-War.content:
The Third War


                  
                  Years 23–25 ADP 
                  
                

The Scourge destroyed Lordaeron and Quel’Thalas from the inside, the Burning Legion returned, and the world was saved by an alliance nobody wanted, on a mountain nobody could defend.
What Happened

A plague spreads through northern Lordaeron, turning the dead into Scourge. Prince Arthas Menethil investigates with Jaina Proudmoore and Uther the Lightbringer.
Arthas culls Stratholme — slaughtering his own infected citizens before they can turn. Uther refuses. Arthas disbands the Order of the Silver Hand on the spot.
Arthas sails to Northrend, burns his own ships, and takes up the runeblade Frostmourne. It takes his soul.
Arthas returns and murders his father, King Terenas. Lordaeron falls.
Arthas cuts the Dead Scar through Quel’Thalas and defiles the Sunwell to raise Kel’Thuzad as a lich, who summons Archimonde.
Archimonde destroys Dalaran.
Medivh, returned as a prophet, warns the leaders to flee west. Only Jaina Proudmoore and Thrall listen.
In Kalimdor, Grom Hellscream drinks demon blood again to kill Mannoroth — and in dying, breaks the orcs’ blood curse forever.
The Battle of Mount Hyjal: humans, orcs, and night elves stand together. Nordrassil’s power is detonated to destroy Archimonde. The night elves lose their immortality.
Aftermath: Illidan Stormrage flees to Outland. Sylvanas Windrunner frees herself and founds the Forsaken. Kael’thas Sunstrider leads the Blood Elves away. Arthas merges with Ner’zhul to become the whole Lich King.

Why It Still Matters
Everything in the present tense is Third War wreckage. The Plaguelands, the Forsaken, Theramore, Durotar, Teldrassil, the broken Silver Hand, the Scarlet Crusade, the fragile Alliance–Horde non-aggression — all of it. Four years ago. Everyone at the table remembers it.
Related
Arthas Menethil · The Lich King · Mount Hyjal · Scourge · Sylvanas Windrunner · Thrall · Jaina Proudmoore · The Four Years After

Lore/History/The-Troll-Wars.title: The Troll Wars
Lore/History/The-Troll-Wars.content:
The Troll Wars


                  
                  ~2,700 years before the Dark Portal 
                  
                

The Amani troll empire moved to exterminate the high elves of Quel’Thalas. The elves, badly outnumbered, went to the humans of Arathor for help.
What Happened

The exiled Highborne — now High Elves — had founded Quel’Thalas atop a troll holy site. The Amani took offense, correctly.
Arathor sends its armies. In exchange, the elves teach one hundred humans the arcane arts.
Combined human steel and elven magic breaks the Amani at the gates of Quel’Thalas.

Why It Still Matters
This is the founding alliance of human and elf, and the origin of human magic — which leads directly to Dalaran, the Kirin Tor, the Guardians of Tirisfal, and Medivh opening the Dark Portal. It also leaves the Amani with a grudge that is still burning at launch in the Hinterlands and Eastern Plaguelands.
Related
High Elves · Humans · Trolls · Quel’Thalas · Kirin Tor

Lore/History/The-War-of-the-Ancients.title: The War of the Ancients
Lore/History/The-War-of-the-Ancients.content:
The War of the Ancients


                  
                  ~10,000 years before the Dark Portal 
                  
                

Queen Azshara and her Highborne, drunk on the Well of Eternity, opened a portal for Sargeras. The Burning Legion poured into a world that had never seen war.
What Happened

The Highborne’s reckless spellcraft draws Sargeras’s attention across the Twisting Nether.
Azshara agrees to unmake the world in exchange for godhood. Her court begins widening the portal.
Malfurion Stormrage, taught by Cenarius, leads a resistance of night elves, Dragons, Furbolg, and earthen.
Illidan Stormrage — jealous of his brother, in love with Tyrande Whisperwind — betrays the resistance to Sargeras, and is scarred and given his demonic sight.
Neltharion forges the Demon Soul, drains the other four flights, and turns on everyone. He becomes Deathwing.
The resistance destroys the Well of Eternity to close the portal.

Why It Still Matters
Everything after is aftershock. The Sundering, the Naga, the exile of the Highborne, the founding of Quel’Thalas, the broken Dragon Aspects, Deathwing’s existence, and the night elves’ ten-thousand-year isolation all begin here. It is also the Legion’s first failure — and they do not forget.
Related
The Sundering · Queen Azshara · Illidan Stormrage · Malfurion Stormrage · Deathwing · Night Elves · Arcane Magic and the Well of Eternity

Lore/History/The-War-of-the-Shifting-San.title: The War of the Shifting Sands
Lore/History/The-War-of-the-Shifting-San.content:
The War of the Shifting Sands


                  
                  ~1,000 years before the Dark Portal 
                  
                

The qiraji erupted from Ahn’Qiraj and nearly took Kalimdor. It ended not in victory but in a wall.
What Happened

The insectoid qiraji, servants of the Old God C’Thun, pour out of the buried city of Ahn’Qiraj into Silithus and beyond.
The Night Elves under Fandral Staghelm fight them to a standstill at terrible cost. Staghelm’s son Valstann is killed in front of him.
The Bronze Dragonflight under Anachronos intervenes. Dragons die.
Unable to destroy the enemy, the dragons and night elves raise the Scarab Wall and seal the gates of Ahn’Qiraj. Anachronos leaves the Scepter of the Shifting Sands as the only key — then shatters it.

Why It Still Matters
The war was never won. It was paused. At launch the wall still stands, the qiraji are still inside, and the Twilight’s Hammer are excavating in Silithus trying to help them out. Fandral Staghelm’s grief over Valstann is the crack in the Cenarion Circle’s leadership.
Related
Ahn’Qiraj · C’Thun · Silithus · Fandral Staghelm · Bronze Dragonflight · Twilight’s Hammer

Lore/Peoples/Blood-Elves.title: Blood Elves
Lore/Peoples/Blood-Elves.content:
Blood Elves


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

The high elves who chose survival over dignity, took a new name, and left. They are not here.


After the fall of Quel’Thalas, Kael’thas Sunstrider renamed his people sin’dorei — children of blood — in memory of the dead, and led them in search of a cure for their arcane withdrawal. They went through the Dark Portal into Outland, where they have fallen in with Illidan Stormrage.
Related
High Elves · Kael’thas Sunstrider · Quel’Thalas · Illidan Stormrage · Playable Species at Launch · Canon Boundary — What Exists at Launch

Lore/Peoples/Centaur.title: Centaur
Lore/Peoples/Centaur.content:
Centaur


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

Born of a demigod’s terrible mistake, and at war with everyone including themselves.


The centaur are the offspring of Zaetar, son of Cenarius, and Princess Theradras, an earth elemental princess and daughter of Therazane. Their birth killed their father. Cenarius disowned them.
They spread across Desolace, Thousand Needles, and the Barrens, and hunted the Tauren to the brink until Thrall’s orcs intervened.
The Clans
Five khanates, perpetually at war with each other. At launch the two accessible ones are:

Gelkis Clan (Desolace) — will deal with outsiders who kill Magram
Magram Clan (Desolace) — will deal with outsiders who kill Gelkis

Also present: the Kolkar (Barrens, Desolace), the Galak (Thousand Needles), the Maraudine (Maraudon).
Theradras herself lies at the heart of Maraudon, mourning Zaetar and corrupting the earth around her.
Related
Maraudon · Desolace · Cenarius · Tauren · Princess Theradras · Reputation as a Mechanic

Lore/Peoples/Dark-Iron-Dwarves.title: Dark Iron Dwarves
Lore/Peoples/Dark-Iron-Dwarves.content:
Dark Iron Dwarves


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

The clan that lost the civil war, summoned a fire god out of spite, and has been his property ever since.


One of the three dwarven clans of the War of the Three Hammers. Defeated and exiled, the Dark Iron under the sorcerer-thane Thaurissan retreated to Blackrock Mountain and summoned Ragnaros the Firelord to win their war for them.
Ragnaros came. He obliterated their city, raised Blackrock Mountain in the process, and enslaved them all.
They consider this a reasonable trade.
At Launch

Emperor Dagran Thaurissan rules the Dark Iron from the Imperial Seat in Blackrock Depths
He has abducted and married Princess Moira Bronzebeard, Magni Bronzebeard’s only daughter — and she may not want rescuing
The Shadowforge city sprawls beneath the mountain; Molten Core lies below it
They are actively working to widen the summoning that binds Ragnaros
Dark Iron agents operate in Searing Gorge, Burning Steppes, Wetlands (Dun Modr), and Redridge Mountains

Related
Blackrock Mountain · Blackrock Depths · Ragnaros · Dagran Thaurissan · Magni Bronzebeard · Molten Core · Dwarves

Lore/Peoples/Darkspear-Trolls.title: Darkspear Trolls
Lore/Peoples/Darkspear-Trolls.content:
Darkspear Trolls


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A small, displaced tribe who owe the Horde everything, and who are the only trolls on Azeroth that anybody trusts.


Playable: Yes · Faction: Horde · Homeland: Durotar / the Echo Isles · Capital: (guests in Orgrimmar) · Leader: Vol’jin
Where They Stand
The Darkspear were a dwindling jungle tribe on the Broken Isles, being eaten alive by Murlocs and a sea witch (Zar’jira), when Thrall’s fleet ran aground nearby. The orcs saved them; the trolls’ witch doctor Sen’jin died in the fighting. His son Vol’jin brought the survivors into the Horde and has led them since.
They were given the Echo Isles off Durotar — and then lost them to Zalazane, a Darkspear witch doctor who went mad, seized the islands, and enslaved his own tribesmen with voodoo. The Darkspear now live in Sen’jin Village on the Durotar coast and as guests in Orgrimmar’s Valley of Spirits.
Trolls In General
Most trolls are hostile: the Amani (Eastern Plaguelands, Hinterlands), the Gurubashi (Stranglethorn Vale), the Sandfury (Tanaris), the Frostmane (Dun Morogh), the Witherbark (Arathi Highlands), the Atal’ai (Swamp of Sorrows). Troll empires once covered both continents; every other civilization is squatting on their ruins, and they are all, without exception, extremely annoyed about it.
The Darkspear are the exception, and other trolls consider them traitors.
Voodoo
Darkspear spirituality is loa-worship and shadow magic — spirits bargained with rather than gods worshipped. It sits uneasily beside orcish shamanism and tauren ancestor-faith, and Thrall has decided not to ask too many questions.
Character Traits

Regenerative — trolls heal from wounds that would kill anyone else. Severed limbs regrow, slowly.
Wry and fatalistic — the Darkspear have a sense of humor about their circumstances
Cannibalism is traditional — and quietly practiced, and the other Horde races prefer not to discuss it
Loyal absolutely to Vol’jin and Thrall — this is a tribe that knows what it owes

Playing One
A Darkspear PC has the tightest, most personal starting motivation in the Horde: go home. Zalazane holds the Echo Isles and some of their family are still there, enthralled.
Related
Vol’jin · Durotar · Orgrimmar · Trolls · Thrall · Stranglethorn Vale

Lore/Peoples/Dwarves.title: Dwarves
Lore/Peoples/Dwarves.content:
Dwarves


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

Miners, drinkers, and unexpectedly the species with the most disturbing origin story on the continent.


Playable: Yes · Faction: Alliance · Homeland: Dun Morogh · Capital: Ironforge · Leader: King Magni Bronzebeard
Where They Stand
Ironforge is the Alliance’s most functional institution — a mountain-city under Dun Morogh that has fed, armed, and sheltered every ally who asked. It currently shelters the entire gnomish nation in Tinker Town, and does not complain about it.
The Three Hammers
Dwarven unity ended in a civil war three centuries ago. Three clans, three claims:

























ClanWhereStatusBronzebeardIronforgeWon. Rule the mountain.Wildhammer ClanAerie Peak, The HinterlandsExiled north. Gryphon-riders. Alliance-friendly but not Alliance-subject.Dark Iron DwarvesBlackrock MountainExiled, summoned Ragnaros, now enslaved to him. Enemies.
The Revelation
Character Traits

Archaeological obsession — the Explorers’ League digs everywhere, invited or not
Clan loyalty over national loyalty — a Wildhammer’s first duty is to Aerie Peak
Hard-drinking, hard-working, genuinely warm — dwarves like people
Devout — dwarven paladins are pragmatic rather than pious

Playing One
Dwarf PCs get built-in purpose: the Explorers’ League will fund an expedition anywhere. A Bronzebeard, a Wildhammer, or — with real justification — a Dark Iron defector are all viable. The Uldaman question can be personal.
Related
Ironforge · Magni Bronzebeard · Uldaman · Earthen · The Titans · Dark Iron Dwarves · Wildhammer Clan · Explorers’ League

Lore/Peoples/Earthen.title: Earthen
Lore/Peoples/Earthen.content:
Earthen


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

What the dwarves were before they were dwarves: living stone, made by the Titans, and still sleeping in vaults under the world.


The Earthen were titan-forged constructs of animate rock, created to shape Azeroth’s crust. The Curse of Flesh — a lingering Old God corruption — transformed them into the mortal, breathing, hairy people now called Dwarves.
Some never woke. Some never changed. Earthen and their stone-kin still stand dormant in Titan vaults, most notably Uldaman in the Badlands, where Archaedas and Ironaya guard the archives.

Lore/Peoples/Forsaken.title: Forsaken
Lore/Peoples/Forsaken.content:
Forsaken


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

Undead who broke the Lich King’s hold and got their minds back — and have discovered that having your mind back is not the same as having your life back.


Playable: Yes · Faction: Horde · Homeland: Tirisfal Glades · Capital: Undercity · Leader: Banshee Queen Sylvanas Windrunner
Where They Stand
When Arthas’s power over the Scourge weakened after The Third War, Sylvanas Windrunner — the ranger-general he had murdered and raised as a banshee — seized her own free will and took a large portion of the undead with her.
They call themselves the Forsaken: not Scourge, not alive, not anyone’s.
They hold Tirisfal Glades and built Undercity in the catacombs beneath the ruins of Lordaeron’s Capital City — directly under the throne room where Arthas killed his father.
Their Position

Hated by the Alliance, who see them as Scourge with better manners and are not entirely wrong
Tolerated by the Horde — Thrall accepted them out of pragmatism. Cairne Bloodhoof objected and was overruled. The tauren still object.
At war with the Scourge, permanently and existentially
At war with the Scarlet Crusade, who consider them the enemy — which is also not entirely wrong

What They Are
The Forsaken do not eat, sleep, breathe, or age. They rot slowly and can be repaired. Their bodies are wrong and they know it. Some remember their living families and cannot approach them. Some are trying very hard to remain the person they were. Some have stopped trying.
Character Traits

Grim, dry, unsentimental humor — it is the only functional coping mechanism
Free will is sacred — nothing terrifies a Forsaken like the idea of being controlled again
Pragmatic to the point of atrocity — they have nothing left to lose and it shows
Not evil, and not good — the Forsaken are the campaign’s best moral grey zone

Playing One
A Forsaken PC can play the horror straight: someone with a family in Southshore who thinks they’re dead, someone slowly deciding whether the person they were is worth preserving. The Horde is a flag of convenience, not a home.
Related
Sylvanas Windrunner · Undercity · Tirisfal Glades · Scourge · Scarlet Crusade · The Third War · Royal Apothecary Society

Lore/Peoples/Furbolg.content:
Furbolg


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

Peaceful ursine shamanists who were the night elves’ oldest allies — and most of whom have now gone violently insane.


Furbolg tribes have lived alongside the Night Elves since before The Sundering and fought beside them in The War of the Ancients.
Then The Third War happened, and demonic corruption spread through their tribes like a disease.

Lore/Peoples/Gnolls.title: Gnolls
Lore/Peoples/Gnolls.content:
Gnolls


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

Hyena-men. Everywhere. Always stealing something.


Scavenging pack-hunters found across both continents, organized into clans of varying competence. They are the default low-level threat in Alliance territory and are more dangerous in numbers than any individual gnoll suggests.
Riverpaw (Elwynn Forest, Westfall) · Redridge (Redridge Mountains) · Mosshide (Wetlands) · Woodpaw (Feralas) · Shadowhide (Redridge Mountains) · Palemane (Mulgore) · Rot Hide (Silverpine Forest — plagued, working for the Scourge)


                  
                  The Rot Hide exception 
                  
                

Rot Hide gnolls in Silverpine have been deliberately infected with the plague of undeath by Scourge necromancers. They are the one gnoll group with a plot attached.

Elwynn Forest · Westfall · Redridge Mountains · Silverpine Forest · Scourge

Lore/Peoples/Gnomes.title: Gnomes
Lore/Peoples/Gnomes.content:
Gnomes


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A nation of refugees who lost their entire country to a betrayal and an engineering decision, and who remain relentlessly, offensively cheerful about it.


Playable: Yes · Faction: Alliance · Homeland: Dun Morogh (Gnomeregan, lost) · Capital: (exiled to Ironforge) · Leader: High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque
Where They Stand
They have no home. Gnomeregan — the great subterranean techno-city beneath Dun Morogh — fell four years ago, and the story is worse than an invasion.
The survivors live in Tinker Town in Ironforge, guests of King Magni Bronzebeard, and are working on getting their city back.
Technology
Gnomish engineering is distinct from goblin engineering: more ambitious, better documented, and it fails differently. Gnomes build things that shouldn’t work and are astonished when they don’t. Goblins build things that shouldn’t work and are astonished when they do.
Character Traits

Irrepressible — a gnome’s optimism is a survival adaptation and it is load-bearing
Precise — they measure things nobody asked them to measure
Engineering, always — even gnome mages and warlocks tinker
Quietly grieving — every adult gnome lost most of their family. They do not talk about it.

Playing One
Gnome PCs have an unimpeachable motivation: retake Gnomeregan. Mekkatorque will personally back an expedition. A gnome who was in the city when the radiation came is a character with something to say.
Related
Gnomeregan · Gelbin Mekkatorque · Sicco Thermaplugg · Ironforge · Professions and Crafting · Dun Morogh

Lore/Peoples/Goblins.title: Goblins
Lore/Peoples/Goblins.content:
Goblins


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

Neutral by policy, mercenary by nature, and the only people on Azeroth to whom the Alliance–Horde war is primarily a market opportunity.


Once slaves of the Ogres on the Isle of Kezan, the goblins were transformed by exposure to kaja’mite ore, which made them brilliant, greedy, and permanently overexcited.
The Steamwheedle Cartel enforces strict neutrality in its port towns — Booty Bay, Gadgetzan, Everlook, Ratchet — where Alliance and Horde drink at the same bar under threat of the Cartel’s very serious bruisers. Violence in a goblin town is bad for business, and goblins deal with bad-for-business decisively.
Not all goblins are Steamwheedle. The Venture Company strip-mines Kalimdor with no regard for anything. The Bilgewater and other cartels freelance. The Blackwater Raiders run Booty Bay’s docks.
At the Table
Goblins are the campaign’s comic relief and its logistics. They sell transport, explosives, information, and each other. A goblin patron is the easiest way to give a cross-faction party a reason to exist.
Related
Steamwheedle Cartel · Venture Company · Booty Bay · Gadgetzan · Professions and Crafting · Travel and Downtime

Lore/Peoples/Harpies.title: Harpies
Lore/Peoples/Harpies.content:
Harpies


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

Winged, screaming, and the only people in Kalimdor that even the centaur avoid.


All-female avian humanoids, universally hostile, nesting in the highlands of Kalimdor. Their origin is disputed — night elf legend blames a curse; they are not answering questions.
Bloodfury (Stonetalon Mountains) · Witchwing (The Barrens) · Dustwind (Thousand Needles) · Frayfeather (Feralas) · Wildmane (Feralas) · Screeching (Desolace)

Lore/Peoples/High-Elves.title: High Elves
Lore/Peoples/High-Elves.content:
High Elves


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A people reduced by ninety percent in a single afternoon, now scattered, addicted, and split over what to do about it.


Descendants of the Highborne exiled from Kalimdor after The Sundering. They founded Quel’Thalas and created the Sunwell from a stolen vial of the Well of Eternity. Their alliance with humanity dates to The Troll Wars, and they taught the first human mages.
In The Third War, Arthas Menethil cut the Dead Scar through their kingdom to reach the Sunwell and defiled it to raise Kel’Thuzad. Nine in ten high elves died.
The Split

Blood Elves — the majority, who took the name sin’dorei in mourning and followed Kael’thas Sunstrider through the Dark Portal to feed their arcane addiction. Offscreen at launch.
High elves proper — the remnant who refused Kael’thas. Some remain with the Alliance: survivors of Dalaran and the Kirin Tor, a delegation in Stormwind City, the rangers at Quel’Danil Lodge in The Hinterlands, and Ambermill in Silverpine Forest. Many are bitter about the Alliance’s slow response when their kingdom burned.

Arcane Withdrawal
Both branches are physically dependent on ambient arcane energy and the Sunwell is gone. The high elves endure it. The blood elves have decided to solve it, by any means.
Related
Quel’Thalas · Blood Elves · Kael’thas Sunstrider · Sylvanas Windrunner · Kirin Tor · Arcane Magic and the Well of Eternity · Playable Species at Launch

Lore/Peoples/Humans.title: Humans
Lore/Peoples/Humans.content:
Humans


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

Short-lived, stubborn, politically incoherent, and somehow still the Alliance’s center of gravity.


Playable: Yes · Faction: Alliance · Homeland: Elwynn Forest · Capital: Stormwind City · Leader: King Anduin Wrynn (child), Bolvar Fordragon as regent
Where They Stand
The human kingdoms of Arathor fragmented eleven centuries ago into seven states, and the last thirty years have been an unbroken run of catastrophe. Stormwind fell to the orcs and was rebuilt. Lordaeron was destroyed by its own crown prince. Alterac was dissolved for treason. Dalaran is a crater. Gilneas has sealed itself behind the Greymane Wall and stopped answering letters. Stromgarde is a contested ruin. Kul Tiras has withdrawn in fury since Admiral Proudmoore’s death.
What remains is Stormwind — ruled by a ten-year-old boy, a regent doing his honest best, and a black dragon.
Faith and Magic
Humans invented nothing and adopted everything. The arcane came from the High Elves after The Troll Wars. The paladin orders were founded in the Second War. The Holy Light is the one thing genuinely theirs, and it just watched its greatest champion become the Lich King.
Character Traits

Adaptable — the only species with mages, paladins, priests, warriors, warlocks, and rogues
Short memory, long grudges — three generations is ancient history, but the Defias debt is unforgiven
Institutional — humans build guilds, orders, churches, and bureaucracies compulsively
Diplomatic by necessity — they are the weakest individually and know it

Playing One
The default outsider’s-eye view of Azeroth. A human PC can be a Stormwind loyalist, a Lordaeron refugee with nothing left, a Kul Tiran sailor with a grudge against Jaina, an Alterac exile living down the treason, or a Gilnean who got out before the wall closed. Each is a different campaign.
Related
Stormwind City · Anduin Wrynn · Bolvar Fordragon · Onyxia · The Holy Light · Defias Brotherhood · Lordaeron

Lore/Peoples/Kobolds.title: Kobolds
Lore/Peoples/Kobolds.content:
Kobolds


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

“You no take candle!”


Small, rat-like, candle-wearing subterranean scavengers who infest every mine on the Eastern Kingdoms. Cowardly individually, dangerous in the dark and in numbers.
They are the first thing most adventurers ever kill, and vanilla’s most quotable enemy. Found in Elwynn Forest (Fargodeep and Jasperlode mines), Dun Morogh, Redridge Mountains, and essentially any hole in the ground.
