Elwynn Forest · Dun Morogh · Bestiary MOC

Lore/Peoples/Murlocs.title: Murlocs
Lore/Peoples/Murlocs.content:
Murlocs


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

Amphibious, incomprehensible, and they always, always bring friends.


Bipedal fish-people infesting every coastline, lake, and marsh on both continents. Their language is untranslated. Their society is unstudied. Their aggression is total.
Notable for two things: the noise (an unmistakable gurgling shriek that means at least four more are coming), and the fact that they were the immediate threat driving the Darkspear Trolls to extinction before Thrall intervened.
Related
Darkspear Trolls · Westfall · Darkshore · Dustwallow Marsh

Lore/Peoples/Naga.title: Naga
Lore/Peoples/Naga.content:
Naga


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

Queen Azshara’s drowned court, ten thousand years underwater, and they have not gotten over it.


When The Sundering pulled the Kaldorei capital beneath the sea, Queen Azshara and her Highborne struck a bargain with a power in the deep — almost certainly an Old God — and were transformed into serpentine immortals.
They have spent ten millennia in the Maelstrom. They are now, for the first time, coming back up.
Where They Surface at Launch
Darkshore · Azshara (the zone) · Desolace (Sar’theris Strand) · Stranglethorn Vale (the Cape) · Blackfathom Deeps · Feralas (Isle of Dread) · Dustwallow Marsh


                  
                  What they want is not clear 
                  
                

Naga incursions at launch look like raids and reconnaissance rather than invasion. Lady Vashj has taken a large contingent to Outland to serve Illidan Stormrage. What Azshara herself wants is unknown and unknowable in 2004 — she has not been seen.


They are excellent as a mystery: the party keeps finding naga in places naga should not be, and nobody can explain the pattern.
Related
Queen Azshara · Azshara (zone) · The Sundering · Blackfathom Deeps · Darkshore · The Old Gods · Lady Vashj

Lore/Peoples/Night-Elves.title: Night Elves
Lore/Peoples/Night-Elves.content:
Night Elves


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

Ten thousand years of immortality, spent four winters ago to kill one demon. They are still processing it.


Playable: Yes · Faction: Alliance · Homeland: Teldrassil · Capital: Darnassus · Leader: High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind
Where They Stand
The Kaldorei survived The Sundering by withdrawing from the world entirely — ten millennia of isolation in Ashenvale and beyond, guarding Nordrassil, sleeping in barrow dens, and forgetting how to negotiate.
Then The Third War came to their door, and they detonated their World Tree to destroy Archimonde.
The Fractured Leadership

Tyrande Whisperwind rules alone and decided, largely by herself, to join the Alliance.
Malfurion Stormrage — her partner, the first druid — is lost in The Emerald Dream. His body sleeps.
Fandral Staghelm leads the Cenarion Circle in Malfurion’s absence. He grew Teldrassil against the Dragon Aspects’ advice, refused their blessing, and the tree is already corrupting. He lost his son at The War of the Shifting Sands and something in him did not come back.
Illidan Stormrage — Malfurion’s twin, released after ten thousand years, fled to Outland. Unfinished business.

Society
Matriarchal. The Sentinels (military) and the Sisters of Elune (priesthood) are women’s institutions; the Cenarion Circle (druids) was men’s until recently. Worship of Elune, the moon goddess, is universal and sincere.
Character Traits

Xenophobic, and working on it — the Alliance is four years old and feels like a compromise
Deeply hostile to arcane magic — it destroyed their empire. Mage is not a night elf option and that is policy.
Ecological absolutism — Horde logging in Ashenvale is not a trade dispute, it is desecration
Patient to the point of paralysis — a decade is a short time to consider something

Playing One
The best night elf PCs are the ones caught between eras: a Sentinel who fought at Hyjal and cannot understand why the war didn’t end, a young druid who has never known immortality, a scholar who suspects Staghelm is wrong about Teldrassil.
Related
Teldrassil · Darnassus · Tyrande Whisperwind · Malfurion Stormrage · Fandral Staghelm · Cenarion Circle · The Emerald Dream · The Sundering · Ashenvale

Lore/Peoples/Ogres.title: Ogres
Lore/Peoples/Ogres.content:
Ogres


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

Draenor’s other export. Big, stupid, occasionally two-headed, and occasionally the smartest thing in the room.


Ogres came to Azeroth with the orcish Horde through the Dark Portal, and stayed after it lost. Some remain allied to orcish remnants; most have gone feral and set up as bandits and warlords.
Ogre magi — often two-headed — are the exception: intelligent, spellcasting, and dangerous. The Gordunni in Feralas are the most organized.
Where They Are
Feralas (Gordunni) · Arathi Highlands (Boulderfist) · Alterac Mountains (Crushridge) · Dustwallow Marsh (Brackenwall — Horde-allied) · Blasted Lands (Dreadmaul) · Stranglethorn Vale (Mosh’Ogg) · Burning Steppes · Dire Maul (post-launch)
Related
Feralas · Dustwallow Marsh · Arathi Highlands · Goblins · Dark Portal

Lore/Peoples/Orcs.title: Orcs
Lore/Peoples/Orcs.content:
Orcs


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A people who were made into a weapon, used, discarded, caged, and who are now — for the first time in three generations — free and sober and trying to work out who they actually are.


Playable: Yes · Faction: Horde · Homeland: Durotar · Capital: Orgrimmar · Leader: Warchief Thrall
Where They Stand
Orcs are not from Azeroth. They are from Draenor, where they were shamanic clan-people until Kil’jaeden and Gul’dan fed them Mannoroth’s blood and turned them into an army. The red skin, the rage, the atrocities of the First and Second Wars — all of it was the curse.
Grom Hellscream broke it. At Demon Fall Canyon in Ashenvale, he drank the demon blood one final time to gain the strength to kill Mannoroth — and killed the curse with him. He died doing it. Orc skin has been fading from red toward brown ever since, and orcish children born since are the first free generation in living memory.
Thrall’s Horde
Thrall was born in an internment camp and raised as a human noble’s gladiator. He escaped, found the Frostwolf clan, learned shamanism from Drek’Thar, and rebuilt his people around honor and the elements rather than conquest.


                  
                  This Horde is not that Horde 
                  
                

It includes Tauren, Darkspear Trolls, and the Forsaken. It is a coalition of the dispossessed, not a war machine. Thrall genuinely wants peace with the Alliance. Almost nobody in the Alliance believes him, and a significant number of orcs think he’s gone soft.


Internal Tensions

The Burning Blade cult recruits orcs who miss the strength the demon blood gave them
Warlocks are technically illegal in Orgrimmar and openly practicing in the Cleft of Shadow
Old-guard warriors chafe at Thrall’s restraint
The Dark Horde at Blackrock Spire under Rend Blackhand never accepted Thrall at all

Character Traits

Honor is the organizing principle — lok’tar ogar, victory or death, but honorably
Shamanism restored — a spiritual practice deliberately rebuilt from near-extinction
Deeply defensive about the past — every orc knows what their fathers did
Blunt — orcish culture prizes directness to a degree other species find alarming

Playing One
The central orc question is what does a warrior culture do when the war is over. A Frostwolf loyalist, a Warsong veteran who misses Ashenvale, a young orc born free and impatient with elders’ guilt, or a shaman rebuilding a broken tradition are all strong.
Related
Thrall · Orgrimmar · Durotar · Grom Hellscream · Mannoroth · The Elemental Planes · Burning Blade · The Interbellum

Lore/Peoples/Quilboar.title: Quilboar
Lore/Peoples/Quilboar.content:
Quilboar


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

Boar-men grown from the blood of a slain demigod, defending shrines nobody else considers sacred.


The quilboar sprang from the corpse of Agamaggan, the great boar demigod who died fighting the Burning Legion in The War of the Ancients. Where his blood fell, thorns grew — and from the thorns, quilboar.
They hold the razorfen thickets of the Barrens and are aggressively territorial.

                  Not simply monsters 
                  
                

The quilboar are defending a holy site from grave-robbers, and the grave-robbers are the player characters. Razorfen Downs in particular is a tragedy — the Death’s Head tribe were losing to the Scourge and turned to necromancy to survive it.

Lore/Peoples/Satyr.title: Satyr
Lore/Peoples/Satyr.content:
Satyr


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

Night elves who accepted Sargeras’s offer, and got exactly what they asked for.


During The War of the Ancients, some Highborne swore themselves to the Burning Legion and were transformed into demonic satyrs. The first and greatest was Xavius, Azshara’s counselor.
They have persisted for ten thousand years, and they are the Night Elves’ most personal shame — because every satyr was once kin.
Where They Are
Ashenvale (Xavian, the Shrine of Aessina) · Felwood (Jaedenar, Shatter Scar Vale) · Azshara (Legash Encampment) · Desolace · Feralas · Darkshore
They practice fel magic, keep Furbolg and night elf captives, and are usually found working toward some larger demonic project — most notably at Jaedenar in Felwood, where they serve the Shadow Council.
Related

Lore/Peoples/Silithid.title: Silithid
Lore/Peoples/Silithid.content:
Silithid


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

Insectoid horrors that are neither animals nor an infestation, but an army — and their masters are still sealed under the sand.


The silithid are the drone-caste of the buried empire of Ahn’Qiraj, servants of the Old God C’Thun. They erupted once before, in The War of the Shifting Sands, and were sealed behind the Scarab Wall.
They are seeping out again through hive mounds across the southern deserts.
Where
Silithus (Hive’Ashi, Hive’Regal, Hive’Zora) · Tanaris (the Gaping Chasm) · Un’Goro Crater (the Slithering Scar) · Thousand Needles
Above the drones sit the qiraji — intelligent, armored, and directing. Above them, C’Thun.
Related
Ahn’Qiraj · C’Thun · Silithus · Twilight’s Hammer · The War of the Shifting Sands

Lore/Peoples/Tauren.title: Tauren
Lore/Peoples/Tauren.content:
Tauren


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

The Horde’s conscience — a nomadic people who just stopped being nomadic, and who are the only faction leadership in the world that everyone trusts.


Playable: Yes · Faction: Horde · Homeland: Mulgore · Capital: Thunder Bluff · Leader: High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof
Where They Stand
The tauren were scattered nomads hunted across the Barrens by the Centaur until Thrall’s orcs helped Cairne Bloodhoof drive them off. Cairne repaid that debt by bringing his people into the Horde, and has never once regretted it — though he has frequently disagreed with it.
Thunder Bluff on the mesas of Mulgore is four years old and is already the most peaceful place on either continent. It is neutral ground where even Alliance emissaries have been received.
Faith
The Earthmother, whose eyes are the sun (An’she) and the moon (Mu’sha). Tauren spirituality is ancestor-facing, land-facing, and genuinely central to daily life — not decoration. Tauren druids were taught by Cenarius himself, and the tauren have joined the Cenarion Circle as full partners with the night elves, which is one of the few genuinely warm cross-faction relationships in the world.
Internal Tension
The Cairne Question
Cairne is the only leader in the world who is on speaking terms with almost everyone — Thrall’s mentor, respected by Jaina Proudmoore, honored by the night elf druids, and the one voice who consistently objected to the Forsaken joining the Horde. He is the campaign’s best neutral arbiter.
Character Traits

Deliberate — tauren do not hurry, and find it strange that others do
Honor the kill — hunting is sacramental; waste is obscene
Communal — the tribe decides, elders are heard, individuals matter less
Physically enormous — tauren are the largest playable people and rooms are built wrong for them

Playing One
Tauren PCs are natural mediators and natural druids. A hunter avenging the Venture Company’s strip-mining, a druid working with night elves, or a young Grimtotem who does not agree with Magatha all have room to move.
Related
Cairne Bloodhoof · Thunder Bluff · Mulgore · Cenarion Circle · Magatha Grimtotem · Centaur · Thrall

Lore/Peoples/Trolls.title: Trolls
Lore/Peoples/Trolls.content:
Trolls


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

The first civilization on Azeroth, and every ruin you have ever looted used to be theirs.


Troll empires — the Gurubashi in the south, the Amani in the north, the Drakkari in Northrend, the Zandalari presiding over all of them — covered Azeroth before elves, before humans, before dwarves. Everything since has been decline.
Trolls are ferociously regenerative, practice voodoo and loa-worship, and hold grudges measured in millennia.

Places/Capitals/Darnassus.title: Darnassus
Places/Capitals/Darnassus.content:
Darnassus


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

There is no ground. The whole city is built in the branches of a tree the size of a mountain range, lit silver, and the only sound is water and wind through leaves.


Faction: Alliance · Ruler: High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind
The night elf capital, grown into the branches of Teldrassil — a city four years old belonging to a people ten thousand years old.
Tyrande Whisperwind rules essentially alone. Malfurion Stormrage is lost in The Emerald Dream. Fandral Staghelm leads the Cenarion Circle from the Cenarion Enclave and disagrees with her on nearly everything.


                  
                  A capital in mourning 
                  
                

The night elves lost their immortality four years ago and have not culturally processed it. Darnassus is beautiful and it is quiet in a way that isn’t peace.

Places/Capitals/Ironforge.title: Ironforge
Places/Capitals/Ironforge.content:
Ironforge


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

The gate is a hole in a mountain and beyond it the air is hot and smells of coal. The whole city is one vast circular hall around a lake of molten metal, and it never gets dark.


Faction: Alliance · Ruler: King Magni Bronzebeard
The most functional institution in the Alliance. Magni Bronzebeard rules a mountain that has fed, armed, and sheltered every ally who asked — including an entire displaced nation.
The Great Forge at the centre is a lake of molten metal and the source of most Alliance steel. The Deeprun Tram runs from here to Stormwind City beneath the sea, which is a genuine engineering marvel that dwarves and gnomes built together and mention constantly.

Stormwind Cathedral


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

The largest building in the human world, built by masons who were never paid for it.


The Cathedral of Light in Cathedral Square, Stormwind City — the seat of the Church of the Holy Light under Archbishop Benedictus, and the human world’s spiritual centre.
Priests and paladins train here. The Order of the Silver Hand was headquartered here before Arthas disbanded it.


                  
                  The irony is structural 
                  
                

This building was raised by the Stonemasons’ Guild, who were then refused payment and became the Defias Brotherhood. Every service held here happens inside a monument to a debt the crown will not acknowledge.

Alterac Mountains

Snow, ruins, and a violet dome on the horizon that nothing has been able to enter for four years.


Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 30–40 (tabletop 8–10) · Held by: Syndicate, Crushridge ogres — no legitimate authority
A kingdom that was dissolved. Lord Perenolde betrayed the Alliance during The Second War and Alterac was struck from the map. Its nobility became the Syndicate, now led by his son Aliden Perenolde, and they hold the ruins of their own capital as bandits.
Crushridge ogres hold the rest. Ravenholdt Manor — the rogues’ guild — operates from a house in the hills that officially isn’t there.


                  
                  The ruins of Dalaran 
                  
                

The shattered remains of Dalaran lie under a great violet dome of magical energy, raised by surviving Kirin Tor after Archimonde destroyed the city. Nobody gets in. Nobody has explained what the dome is for. It is one of the best pieces of unexplained scenery in the game.

The birthplace of human civilization. Arathor was founded here, and Stromgarde Keep is the last of the seven kingdoms still holding its own ground — barely.
Prince Galen Trollbane commands a garrison fighting the Syndicate for the ruins of his own city and the Boulderfist ogres for everything else. Stromgarde has effectively left the Alliance; it was not invited back after The Second War and it has stopped asking.
Refuge Pointe (Alliance) and Hammerfall (Horde) glare at each other across the middle of the zone. Hammerfall’s orcs are Dragonmaw remnants — the clan that chained Alexstrasza at Grim Batol — now reformed under Thrall, which not everyone believes.

Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 45–55 (tabletop 13–15) · Held by: Nobody. Nethergarde Keep holds a corner.
Thirty years ago this was Black Morass. Then Medivh opened the Dark Portal and the land died in a radius.
The Portal stands dormant — a stone arch with no light in it, watched from Nethergarde Keep by a garrison the Kirin Tor posted a generation ago and never rotated out. They have been waiting for something to come through for thirty years. Nothing has.

Dalaran

A crater under a violet dome the size of a hill. Nothing goes in. Nothing comes out. Nobody will explain what the dome is for.

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Duskwood.title: Duskwood
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Duskwood.content:
Duskwood


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

There is no sun here. Not clouds — the light simply does not arrive. The trees are black, the road is the only safe ground, and something in the treeline is keeping pace with you.


Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 20–30 (tabletop 5–7) · Held by: Nominally Stormwind. In practice, nothing living.
It was called Brightwood once. Then The Third War and a badly-handled summoning turned it into this.
The dead do not stay buried at Raven Hill. Worgen — the Nightbane — hunt the deep woods, released by a spell nobody will admit to casting. Ogres hold Vul’Gol. And the Kingdom of Stormwind, again, has sent nobody.
Darkshire survives on the Night Watch: exhausted volunteers who patrol until they can’t and are led by a commander who is very obviously past breaking.


                  
                  The gothic horror zone 
                  
                

Duskwood runs on personal tragedy rather than politics. Stalvan Mistmantle, the tutor whose obsession destroyed a family. Morbent Fel, the necromancer at the cemetery. Abercrombie, the hermit assembling a body out of parts. Mor’Ladim, a father raised as an undead monster looking for his daughter’s grave. Each is a self-contained short story and they are among the best-written quests in vanilla.

Stratholme — the city Arthas Menethil culled with his own hands — is now split between Baron Rivendare’s undead and the Scarlet Crusade’s Bastion, both of whom hold half a burning ruin and neither of whom will leave.
Light’s Hope Chapel is the Argent Dawn’s seat: a small consecrated building the Scourge has attacked repeatedly and never taken. It is neutral ground for anyone who is bleeding.
Tirion Fordring lives alone in a hut in the eastern hills, exiled from the Order of the Silver Hand years ago for sparing an orc’s life, drinking, and refusing to be the man everyone needs him to be.

The Alliance’s principal western port, in the Wetlands. Ships run from here to Auberdine in Darkshore and Theramore Isle in Dustwallow Marsh.
It is small, damp, constantly under low-grade threat from murlocs and Dark Iron Dwarves at Dun Modr, and absolutely essential — cut Menethil and the Alliance’s two continents come apart.

Nethergarde Keep


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A fortress built to watch a door, garrisoned by people who have been watching it for thirty years, and nothing has ever come through.


A Kirin Tor-founded fortress in the Blasted Lands, established after The Second War to watch the Dark Portal.
The garrison has been on station for a generation. They have never been rotated out. They are still watching.

Quel’Thalas


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A golden forest kingdom with a black scar cut straight through it, from the border to the heart, and nothing grows in the scar.


The High Elves’ kingdom, founded ~6,800 years before the Dark Portal by the Highborne exiled from Kalimdor. Its heart was the Sunwell, created from a stolen vial of the Well of Eternity.
Now

Lakeshire sits on Lake Everstill with a broken bridge, a nervous militia, and a mayor who has written to Stormwind eleven times.
To the east, the Blackrock orcs have taken Stonewatch Keep — a Stormwind fortress — and are massing in Render’s Valley. To the north, gnolls. To the south, more gnolls. The town is surrounded and the crown’s answer has been silence.

Thorium Point is the exception: the Thorium Brotherhood, Dark Iron defectors who rejected Ragnaros and just want to forge. They are neutral, they are the best smiths alive, and they are the party’s supplier if Molten Core is ever on the table.

Silverpine Forest

Shadowfang Keep (22–30 / tabletop 5–7)


The Forsaken’s southern approach, and a zone where three separate problems overlap.
Shadowfang Keep stands above Pyrewood Village, where the archmage Arugal — driven mad after summoning worgen to fight the Scourge — now presides over a castle full of the things he called. The villagers of Pyrewood transform at nightfall.
Rot Hide gnolls have been deliberately infected with the plague by Scourge necromancers. Ambermill holds out as a Dalaran mage enclave. And to the south stands the Greymane Wall, behind which the kingdom of Gilneas sealed itself off decades ago and has not been heard from since.

Stranglethorn Vale

Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 30–45 (tabletop 8–11) · Held by: Contested — nobody, Steamwheedle Cartel in Booty Bay
A vast jungle covering the southern tip of the continent, and the closest thing to genuinely neutral ground on Azeroth.
The Gurubashi empire ruled here and left ziggurats everywhere. Its remnant is fractured: some tribes serve Hakkar the Soulflayer, others fight them. Zul’Gurub stands sealed in the north.
Booty Bay at the southern tip is the Steamwheedle Cartel’s crown jewel: a goblin port where Alliance and Horde drink at the same bar because Baron Revilgaz’s bruisers will throw anyone who fights into the sea.

Stromgarde


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A walled city on cliffs, held by a garrison fighting on three fronts, which was not invited back into the Alliance and has stopped asking.


The last surviving kingdom of Arathor, the original human empire, in the Arathi Highlands.
Prince Galen Trollbane commands what is left, fighting the Syndicate for the ruins of his own city and the Boulderfist ogres for everything outside it.

Western Plaguelands

Scholomance (58–60 / tabletop 18)


Where the plague began. Andorhal was the distribution point — Kel’Thuzad’s Cult of the Damned poisoned the grain here and shipped it across Lordaeron. The lich Araj the Summoner holds the ruins now.
Hearthglen to the north is Scarlet Crusade-held, commanded by Highlord Taelan Fordring — son of the disgraced paladin Tirion Fordring — who is a genuinely good man slowly realizing what he’s part of.

Wetlands


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

It rains. It has been raining for as long as anyone can remember. Raptors call to each other across the fens and the road is the only thing not underwater.


Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 20–30 (tabletop 5–7) · Held by: Contested — Alliance at Menethil, everything else feral
Marshland between the dwarven highlands and the northern coast. Menethil Harbor is the Alliance’s main port for Kalimdor and Theramore Isle, and it is the only reason anyone comes here.
Dun Modr to the north is a ruin held by Dark Iron Dwarves. Whelgar’s Excavation has been overrun by raptors. And to the northwest, across the water, stands Grim Batol — sealed, silent, and the site of one of the worst things that ever happened to a dragon.


                  
                  Grim Batol 
                  
                

Where the Horde chained Alexstrasza with the Demon Soul during The Second War and bred her children into war-mounts. She is free now. The fortress is sealed and nobody goes near it. It is inaccessible at launch and it should stay that way — it’s a piece of dread, not a dungeon.

Ashenvale


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Old forest, blue-green light, and the sound of axes. Not woodcutting axes. Well — yes, woodcutting axes. That’s the problem.

Blackfathom Deeps (24–32 / tabletop 6–7)


The night elves’ ancestral forest, and the hottest front of the faction war — because the Horde is logging it.
The Warsong Outriders cut timber at the Warsong Lumber Camp to build Orgrimmar. The Silverwing Sentinels kill them for it. Neither Thrall nor Tyrande Whisperwind has been able or willing to stop it.


                  
                  Demon Fall Canyon 
                  
                

This is where Grom Hellscream killed Mannoroth and broke the orcish blood curse forever — dying in the act. It is the single most sacred site in orcish history and it is in night elf territory, which neither side has worked out how to handle.

Azshara

The far north-east: the overgrown outskirts of the ancient Highborne capital, named for the queen who destroyed it.
Naga have returned to these coasts in force — the drowned descendants of Queen Azshara’s court, coming home after ten thousand years. Nobody knows why now.
Satyrs hold the Legash Encampment. Blue dragonkin are at the Bay of Storms. And Duke Hydraxis of the Hydraxian Waterlords holds a stretch of coast, offering an alliance to anyone willing to fight Ragnaros.

Durotar

The Echo Isles off the coast belong to the Darkspear Trolls and are held by Zalazane, a witch doctor who went mad and enthralled his own tribe.

Places/Kalimdor/Moonglade.content:
Moonglade


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

A perfect valley. Still water, silver light, and a silence that is not empty but attentive. Alliance and Horde druids pass each other on the path and nod.


Continent: Kalimdor · Levels: 55 (tabletop 17) · Held by: Cenarion Circle — neutral, inviolate
The Cenarion Circle’s seat, and the best neutral ground in the setting.
Druids of both factions train, sleep, and argue here, and the peace is absolute — not enforced by guards but by the fact that nobody who reaches Moonglade wants to break it.
Nighthaven is the settlement. Lake Elune’ara is the centre. The Stormrage Barrow Dens hold sleeping druids, including Malfurion Stormrage — whose body lies here while his spirit is trapped in The Emerald Dream.
Fandral Staghelm presides in his absence, and does not appear to be looking very hard.

Places/Kalimdor/Mount-Hyjal.title: Mount Hyjal
Places/Kalimdor/Mount-Hyjal.content:
Mount Hyjal


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

The mountain where the world was saved, four years ago, and nobody has been allowed back up since.


The highest peak in Kalimdor, holding the second Well of Eternity (created secretly by Illidan Stormrage) and the World Tree Nordrassil grown over it.


                  
                  The Battle of Mount Hyjal 
                  
                

The climax of The Third War. Humans under Jaina Proudmoore, orcs under Thrall, and night elves under Tyrande Whisperwind and Malfurion Stormrage fought together — the only time in history — to hold the mountain against Archimonde.
They lost the battle and won the war: Nordrassil’s power was detonated as Archimonde reached it, destroying him utterly.
The night elves lost their immortality. That was the price and they paid it knowingly.


Now
Nordrassil is damaged. The mountain is inaccessible — closed off, guarded, and not a playable zone until The Burning Crusade. It is the founding memory of the present era and everyone at the table over the age of ten remembers it.

Nordrassil


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

The first World Tree, grown over a stolen well by three dragons, and it is not what it was.


The original World Tree, grown by the Dragon Aspects atop Mount Hyjal over the second Well of Eternity that Illidan Stormrage created.

Continent: Kalimdor · Levels: 48–55 (tabletop 14–16) · Held by: Nobody. It has never been settled.
A vast volcanic crater containing an intact prehistoric ecosystem. Devilsaurs. Diemetradons. Things that should have died out with the Titans and evidently did not, because the Titans kept them.

Un’Goro is Titan machinery. Six elemental pylons ring the crater, still functioning, still doing something. The Explorers’ League at Marshal’s Refuge is trying to work out what. The crystals scattered across the crater floor are part of the mechanism.

Player-Primer-—-Azeroth-in-Year-29.content:
Player Primer — Azeroth in Year 29


                  
                  Safe to share 
                  
                

This is the only document in the vault written for players. Send it before session zero. It contains no secrets, no twists, and nothing a character wouldn’t plausibly know. Everything genuinely hidden has been left out on purpose.



What This Is
A Dungeons & Dragons campaign set in the world of Warcraft — specifically, Azeroth as it stood in 2004, at the moment the original game began. Not the version from the last twenty years of expansions. The early one, when the map was smaller and almost nothing had been settled yet.
You don’t need to have played Warcraft. Genuinely. Roughly half of what a longtime player “knows” about this era was written years later and doesn’t apply here anyway, so everyone starts closer to level than you’d expect.

Where We Are
Four years ago, the world nearly ended.
A demonic army called the Burning Legion invaded. Orcs, humans, and night elves — three peoples with every reason to hate each other — fought together on the slopes of a mountain called Hyjal and stopped it. The night elves spent ten thousand years of immortality to do it. It worked.
Then everyone went home, and nobody agreed what came next.
That’s where we start. Not in a golden age and not in a ruin — in the messy, underfunded, badly-organised aftermath, four years on, where the heroes have scattered and the paperwork was never done.
Some things you’d know if you lived there:

The kingdom of Lordaeron is gone. Not conquered — destroyed from within by an undead plague. Its survivors are refugees. Its capital is a graveyard.
Stormwind still stands, ruled by a ten-year-old king and a regent doing his best. It is broke, and its outlying provinces have noticed that nobody is coming to help them.
Ironforge is rich, stable, and quietly running most of the Alliance because nobody else can afford to.
The orcs have a homeland. For the first time. A red desert on another continent that nobody else wanted, with a city built out of raw timber and iron four years ago.
The night elves are mortal now, for the first time in ten millennia, and they are not handling it well.
There is no war and there is no peace. Alliance and Horde raid each other over lumber, land, and old grudges, in three or four places, constantly, while both leaderships insist it isn’t a war.


The Two Sides
The Alliance isn’t an alliance. It’s seven governments that won a war together, never signed anything afterward, and are currently held together by habit and by Ironforge’s money. Humans, dwarves, gnomes, and — recently and uneasily — night elves.
The Horde isn’t the Horde you may have heard of. The old one was a demon-poisoned war machine. This one is four years old, led by a young shaman who freed his people from prison camps and is trying to build a country out of them. Orcs, trolls, tauren, and the undead who broke free of the plague that made them.
Neither side is the villain. Both have people in them doing indefensible things and people in them trying very hard. If the campaign works, you should at some point find yourself agreeing with someone you’re supposed to be fighting.

Who You Can Be
Human, dwarf, gnome, or night elf on the Alliance side. Orc, troll, tauren, or Forsaken — the free-willed undead — on the Horde side.
We’re using D&D 5.5E, plus the official Warcraft sourcebook when it releases. Bring a character concept to session zero rather than a finished sheet; we’ll settle species, class, and the mechanical details together, and some of it depends on what the book says.
Come with an idea of where your character is from and what they want. That’s more useful than a build.

What Kind Of Game This Is
You start small. Level one, in one place, with local problems — a mine, a missing patrol, a farm that can’t pay its taxes. The world’s larger disasters are all happening, but they’re happening somewhere else for now, and you’ll hear about them long before you can do anything about them.
Violence is one tool. Several of the campaign’s genuine problems can’t be solved by winning a fight — and at least one gets actively worse if you try. Expect documents, negotiations, and people with legitimate grievances alongside the monsters.
Your relationships are your resources. The people you help early will matter later. So will the ones you don’t.
Death is real. No respawns, no running back to your body. Resurrection exists but it’s rare, expensive, and someone will want something for it.

One Request
If you already know Warcraft well: please don’t look things up mid-campaign, and don’t tell the others what’s coming. Several plot threads depend on nobody at the table knowing the answer yet, and a wiki tab will flatten them.
If you know some of it, come tell the DM privately what you know. Being trusted with a secret is much more fun than accidentally spoiling one.

Bring To Session Zero

A character concept — species, rough class idea, and one sentence about what they want
Anything you’d rather the game avoid, or handle carefully. This gets asked properly at the table too.
Questions. Any of them. There’s no such thing as a dumb Warcraft question here — half the table is learning it fresh.

Rules/Death-and-Resurrection.title: Death and Resurrection
Rules/Death-and-Resurrection.content:
Death and Resurrection


                  
                  The ruling 
                  
                

No spirit healers. No corpse runs. No graveyard respawns. Death in this Azeroth works the way death works in D&D 5.5E — and that means it is rare, expensive to undo, and permanent when the party cannot pay.
The videogame’s revolving door is held in reserve as a plot device.



Why This Ruling
Every other system in this vault runs on the assumption that loss is real. The Forsaken are a people defined by having died. Start — Deathknell (Forsaken) opens with a character waking in a box. The Doom Clocks work because consequences stick.
A world with spirit healers on every hilltop has none of that. The moment dying is free, the Scourge stops being frightening.

What Death Costs

























LevelRealistic Recourse1–4Almost none. A cleric of the Order of the Silver Hand or a Cenarion Circle druid might be reachable, and will ask for something the party cannot casually give.5–8Revivify exists in the world but is held by named NPCs, not sold. Getting the body to one in time is an adventure.9–14Raise dead is obtainable in a capital. It costs money, a favour, and a debt — and the recipient carries a penalty for weeks of in-world time. Use a time skip.15+Available to those with standing. The question stops being can we and becomes what do we owe now, and to whom.

The Light Does Not Fix Everything
A useful in-world constraint, and it is period-correct:

The Light cannot restore what has been claimed. Anyone killed by the Scourge and raised by it is beyond ordinary resurrection.
Fel damage scars. Death by demonic means complicates every attempt.
Forsaken PCs are already dead. They do not benefit from resurrection magic at all; restoring a destroyed Forsaken is a different, darker, and entirely unsolved problem. Establish this at session zero with any Forsaken player.

Primary Trades

Dragonscale, elemental, tribal branches.TailoringWeaver’s tools. Bolt-based; mooncloth and shadowcloth need special sites.EnchantingNo 5e analogue — treat as a downtime activity. Potions, elixirs, transmutation.Herbalism / Mining / SkinningGathering. Handle with a check against terrain.
Secondary
First Aid (bandages — a real combat action in vanilla) · Cooking (buff food, campfires) · Fishing (patient, occasionally lucrative)
Rules of Thumb

Specialization is exclusive. Goblin or gnomish engineering, never both. Choosing is characterization.
Recipes are treasure. A pattern from the Thorium Brotherhood is a reward on par with a magic item.
Gathering is a reason to travel. Arcane crystals in Winterspring. Black lotus in Silithus. Thorium in Searing Gorge.
Crafting takes downtime, not a rest. Days, not minutes.

Rules/Travel-and-Downtime.content:
Travel and Downtime


                  
                  Decided at the table 
                  
                

Hearthstones exist, once per week. Flight paths exist and are expensive. Ground mounts are the normal way to cover distance. No spirit healers and no corpse runs — see Death and Resurrection.



Getting Around


















































MethodAvailabilityCost & LimitsFootEveryoneDefault. Small zone: half a day. Large zone: 2–3 days.Ground mountPurchasable from ~tabletop level 4Horse, ram, mechanostrider, saber, wolf, kodo, raptor, skeletal steed. Faction-locked and culturally specific — a dwarf on a kodo is a story.Flight pathBetween known, allied roosts onlyExpensive. Gryphon (Alliance), wyvern (Horde), hippogryph, bat. See pricing below.ShipFixed routes, fixed schedulesMenethil ↔ Theramore ↔ Auberdine ↔ Darnassus · Booty Bay ↔ Ratchet. Days at sea, weather, naga.ZeppelinOrgrimmar ↔ Undercity ↔ Grom’golGoblin-built. This should worry passengers.Deeprun TramStormwind ↔ IronforgeTwo hours, beneath the sea, free. A genuine marvel.HearthstoneOne per character, bound to one innOnce per week. See below.Mage portalMage PCs, or hiredCapitals only. Ruinous if hired at low level.

The Hearthstone
Every character may attune one hearthstone to one inn. Rebinding takes an hour with the innkeeper and can be done anywhere with a bound inn.
Usage: once per seven days. Track it on the character sheet, not in your head — the players will.
Good reasons the stone fails, established in advance and telegraphed:

Deep beneath Blackrock Mountain — the ley interference is audible as a hum
Inside Ahn’Qiraj’s walls or a Titan vault
Aboard a ship at sea, or anywhere in The Emerald Dream
Anywhere the Twilight’s Hammer have prepared ground on purpose


Flight Path Costs
Flight is fast and it should hurt to use. Price it as a real budget decision at levels 1–8, and a convenience by level 12.

























DistanceRough CostFeels LikeOne zone hopSmall but noticeable”Do we need to?”Cross-continent, 3–4 legsA meaningful chunk of party fundsA planned expenseEmergency, unlinked roostRefused at any priceRoosts must be visited on foot first

Time Skips and Artificial Breaks


                  
                  The scheduling tool 
                  
                

The world in The Doom Clocks and World Events Calendar needs time to pass for its consequences to land. The party will not naturally take year-long breaks. So build them in.


Legitimate reasons to skip weeks or months, in rough order of usefulness:








































BreakLengthFictionWinter6–10 weeksPasses close in Dun Morogh. Seas unsafe. Campaigning stops because campaigning does stop.Training2–6 weeksA new tier of ability requires a trainer, a capital, and time. Cover for a level-up.Recovery2–8 weeksA serious wound, a curse, a resurrection debt. See Death and Resurrection.Crafting or commission3–12 weeksResistance gear, a forged weapon, a chartered shipWaiting on the worldanyA trial date, a thaw, a shipment, a birth, a siegePolitical delay4–12 weeksThe Senate votes in spring. The hearing is set for autumn. Nothing the party does moves it.
During a skip, always:

Advance the relevant clocks and read the World Events Calendar for the months crossed.
Give each PC one downtime action (below).
Deliver one piece of bad news the party could have prevented had they been there. Not a punishment — physics.
Change one price. Every clock has an economic shadow.


Downtime Activities
One per character per skip, unless the skip is long.

Craft — see Professions and Crafting
Curry favour — advance a faction’s regard (Reputation as a Mechanic)
Research — libraries in Ironforge, Darnassus, the Kirin Tor in exile, the Explorers’ League
Train — new abilities require a trainer in a capital. This is the usual cover for levelling.
Carouse — Goldshire, the Pig and Whistle, Thelsamar. Roll on Rumor Tables twice and let them keep both.
Work a trade — mercenary contracts, caravan guard, bounties. Pays, and generates hooks.
Tend a relationship — an NPC from Characters MOC. Genuinely the highest-value option and players under-use it. Say so.
